t: Efficient Lossless Compression of Scientific Floating-Point Data on CPUs and GPUs
pb: Scientific datasets are growing faster than storage and interconnect bandwidth, making data compression essential, but existing lossless compressors for floating-point data are either fast or achieve good compression ratios—rarely both simultaneously on both CPUs and GPUs.
me: The paper presents four new lossless compression algorithms specifically designed for single- and double-precision IEEE 754 floating-point data. The algorithms are fully compatible between CPUs and GPUs, enabling the same bitstream to be produced/consumed on either platform. Implementations exploit bit-level patterns in floating-point exponent and mantissa fields to achieve high compression ratios, and are tuned for SIMD/SIMT parallelism to maximize throughput on both CPU vector units and GPU streaming multiprocessors. Evaluated against 18 compressors from the literature on SDRBench scientific datasets.
nv: Four floating-point-specific lossless compression algorithms that are simultaneously CPU/GPU bitstream-compatible and achieve best-in-class throughput (>500 GB/s on RTX 4090) without sacrificing compression ratio.

mx.other: compress+decompress >500 GB/s on RTX 4090; outperforms most of 18 compared compressors in ratio and throughput

th: high-throughput lossless floating-point compression for CPUs and GPUs

t: Design and Technology Co-optimization Utilizing Flip-FET (FFET) Standard Cells
pb: CFET-based standard cells require excessive tap-cell overhead in FEOL to enable backside interconnect routing, hindering efficient use of BEOL backside wiring in sub-3nm nodes.
me: FFET (Flip-FET) flips the lower FET in CFET to enable direct pin accessibility on both BEOL sides without tap-cells. DTCO uses: (1) synthesizing multiple FFET cells with diverse pin distributions, (2) tap-cell-avoiding placement optimization, (3) frontside/backside wire rebalancing.
nv: Flip-FET architecture eliminates tap-cell overhead by enabling dual-sided pin access directly, allowing full exploitation of backside routing.
th: Flip-FET design and technology co-optimization for sub-3nm backside routing

t: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
pb: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
me: Proposes low-cost comparison-free unary number generation mechanism avoiding comparators entirely. Introduces serial and two parallel (exact and approximate) unary generator designs using alternative conversion logic.
nv: Comparison-free unary number generation eliminating comparator overhead in binary-to-unary conversion.
th: Comparison-free unary number generation for efficient data conversion

t: Dynamic Local Usage: An Accurate Model for Usage of Tile-Internal Wiring in Global Routing
pb: Traditional global routing treats local wiring usage as a pre-estimated constant, ignoring actual wire-shape geometry and packing density, leading to inaccuracies in routing prediction and detailed routing failures.
me: Dynamic Local Usage (DLU) model evaluates wiring usage based on exact wire shapes and specific pin geometries. Introduces tip-to-tip penalty extensions for accurate packing density modeling. New routing algorithms optimize routes according to DLU congestion. Supports incremental changes like pin movements.
nv: Exact-geometry-based dynamic local wiring usage model replacing static pre-estimates in global routing.

mx.other: reduced vias, design-rule violations, and timing degradation

th: Dynamic local wiring model for accurate global routing at advanced nodes

t: Secondary-Power-Cell-Aware Detailed Placement in Multiple Power Domain Designs
pb: Cross-domain cells in multi-power-domain designs require secondary power routing that competes with signal routing; strict IR drop constraints at advanced nodes make placement for efficient secondary PDN difficult.
me: Integer linear programming (ILP) model for detailed placement accounting for secondary power routing; targeted adjustments to cross-domain cell placement; validated against commercial tools.
nv: First detailed placement method explicitly optimizing for secondary power distribution network routing in multi-domain designs.
th: Placement optimization for multi-domain secondary power distribution

t: Clearance-Constrained PCB Global Placement with Heterogeneous Components
pb: PCB placement must handle pad-to-pad clearance constraints and heterogeneous components while minimizing routing congestion and overlap.
me: PCB placement framework with: wire-area model accounting for routing resource needs (power/signal nets); pad-to-pad clearance model; two-sided density model for component and pad overlap; quadratic programming-based legalizer resolving violations.
nv: First PCB placement framework explicitly handling pad-to-pad clearance and heterogeneous component geometry.
th: Constraint-aware PCB placement with heterogeneous components

t: Power-Grid Structure Exploration with Unified Sequence-based Learning Framework
pb: Power-grid (PG) structure design at advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm) is critical for power integrity and performance, but design space exploration is complex; initial PG structures dominate optimization space.
me: Proposes a unified framework combining a novel sequence-based structure generator with a Transformer-based voltage-drop predictor. Learned embeddings from the predictor are used to identify promising PG structure candidates on the Pareto frontier during optimization. The sequence-based generator creates candidate PG topologies, while the Transformer predictor estimates static voltage-drop with high accuracy.
nv: First unified framework combining sequence-based PG structure generation with Transformer-based voltage-drop prediction for industrial power-grid optimization.
th: Sequence-based structure generation with Transformer voltage prediction

t: Late Breaking Results: Utilization of Hybrid Threshold-Voltage Flip-flops for Power Recovery
pb: Leakage power reduction in advanced technology nodes is challenging; multi-VT optimization can reduce leakage in non-critical paths, but critical-path sequential cells resist multi-VT optimization due to timing constraints.
me: Introduces hybrid-VT flip-flop cells where master and slave latches use different threshold voltages, allowing independent control of setup time and clock-to-Q delay. This decoupled control enables multi-VT optimization on critical paths without violating timing constraints. Hybrid-VT flip-flops can be applied to designs already optimized with conventional multi-VT cells.
nv: First hybrid-VT flip-flop design enabling independent setup/clock-to-Q control for multi-VT optimization on timing-critical sequential cells.
th: Hybrid-VT flip-flops for leakage reduction on critical paths

t: An Energy-Efficient Kalman Filter Architecture with Tunable Accuracy for Brain-Computer Interfaces
pb: Kalman Filters are standard for BCIs to predict motion from brain activity, but hardware implementations specialized for embedded BCI constraints (latency-accuracy tuning, energy efficiency) are lacking.
me: A configurable KF hardware architecture with tunable latency and accuracy parameters enables design-space exploration for BCI applications; integrated as accelerators into a heterogeneous SoC, supporting efficient neural data processing with dynamic parameter adjustment.
nv: Configurable Kalman Filter hardware architecture enabling fine-grained latency-accuracy tuning for BCI neural signal processing.
th: Configurable Kalman Filter hardware accelerator for brain-computer interfaces

t: Power-Constrained Printed Neuromorphic Hardware Training
pb: Printed neuromorphic circuits (pNCs) must operate under severe power budgets from printed batteries or energy harvesters while maintaining task accuracy; traditional penalty-based optimization requires hundreds of training runs to explore power-accuracy tradeoffs.
me: Augmented Lagrangian optimization enforces task-specific power constraints directly during training, computing optimal power-accuracy tradeoffs in a single run. Tested across 13 benchmarks with different activation functions (p-tanh, p-Clipped_ReLU).
nv: Augmented Lagrangian training approach that directly enforces power constraints and generates full Pareto front in single training run versus penalty-based methods requiring 150+ runs.

mx.other: 52-59x accuracy-to-power improvement; 81.82% accuracy at high power

th: Augmented Lagrangian training for power-constrained printed neuromorphic circuits

t: A Systematic Approach for Multi-objective Double-side Clock Tree Synthesis
pb: As semiconductor devices scale, utilizing back-side silicon space via double-side clock trees requires systematic design resource allocation and multi-objective optimization, but existing tools only hack single-side approaches.
me: The approach performs hierarchical clock routing with concurrent buffers and nano Through-Silicon-Via (nTSV) insertion, followed by skew refinement on double-side metal layers. It systematically allocates resources across back- and front-side, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and via/buffer count through a unified optimization framework.
nv: First systematic multi-objective approach to double-side clock tree synthesis using nTSVs, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and resource utilization rather than adapting single-side heuristics.

mx.other: improved latency, skew, wirelength, reduced buffers and nTSVs vs SOTA

th: double-side clock tree synthesis with nTSVs

t: Late Breaking Results: A Diffusion-Based Framework for Configurable and Realistic Multi-Storage Trace Generation
pb: Existing storage trace generation methods lack the ability to produce realistic, configurable, and diverse multi-device traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies with high fidelity.
me: DiTTO uses diffusion models to synthesize high-fidelity continuous traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies. The framework allows user-defined configurations while maintaining fidelity to real storage patterns, achieving trace generation with only 8% configuration errors.
nv: Application of diffusion-based generative models to multi-storage trace synthesis with configurable parameters and high temporal realism.
th: Diffusion-based generative models for realistic storage workload synthesis

t: STREAM: Spatiotemporal Similarity-based Efficient Approximate Median with Tunable Granularity
pb: Exact median computation is expensive and fails to meet near real-time requirements; existing approximate methods ignore spatiotemporal data characteristics and lack application-specific accuracy-speed trade-offs.
me: STREAM exploits spatiotemporal similarity in data streams to achieve bucket reuse via streaming K-means-like clustering. Introduces tunable-grained bucket mechanism allowing application-specific trade-offs between execution time and accuracy. Uses prior bucket state to accelerate median estimation.
nv: First approximate median algorithm exploiting spatiotemporal data reuse with tunable accuracy-latency knobs.

mx.speedup: 47x vs. DDSketch, 71.2x vs. KLL (10.1x average for both)

th: Spatiotemporal similarity-based approximate median

t: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
pb: GNNs for atomistic materials modeling remain small (millions of parameters) compared to LLMs (billions); lack of scaling guidance limits accuracy and applicability to complex materials discovery tasks.
me: Develops foundational GNN with billions of parameters trained on terabyte-scale datasets; incorporates LLM-inspired training techniques (efficient data/model management) to enable large-scale GNN training and deployment; explores three scaling dimensions: architecture, dataset size, and training method applicability.
nv: First large-scale GNN study (billions of parameters, TB-scale data) for atomistic materials modeling, applying LLM-inspired scaling techniques to GNN architectures.
th: Scaling laws for billion-parameter GNNs in atomistic materials modeling

t: RADiT: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion Transformer Acceleration Leveraging Timestep Similarity
pb: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) require multiple iterative sampling timesteps with redundant computations across consecutive steps, leading to high latency and energy consumption during inference.
me: RADiT identifies data redundancy via blockwise input feature evaluation and skips redundant computations by reusing results from consecutive timesteps. Dynamic Threshold Scaling Module (DTSM) and Compress and Compare Unit (CCU) minimize accuracy degradation while maximizing computational efficiency during redundancy detection.
nv: Timestep-aware redundancy elimination via blockwise feature similarity detection and cross-timestep result reuse with dynamic thresholding.
th: timestep redundancy elimination for diffusion acceleration

t: BS-PDN-Last: Towards Optimal Power Delivery Network Design With Multifunctional Backside Metal Layers
pb: Backside metal layers in advanced chips can serve multiple functions (power delivery, signal routing, thermal); traditional PDN-first design flows reserve these layers for power, leaving suboptimal signal routing and performance trade-offs.
me: BS-PDN-last flow defers power routing to the post-signal routing stage, allowing signal routing to optimize for performance first, then power delivery networks to adapt to remaining backside resources. Uses vector-based IR-drop analysis for accurate power estimation.
nv: Deferring power delivery network design to post-signal routing stage to unlock multifunctional backside utilization and optimize performance-power trade-offs.

mx.other: 90% reduction in Total Negative Slack, 12% performance gain with BS-CDN

th: post-signal-routing power delivery optimization

t: ACRS: Adjacent Computation Resource Sharing among Partitioned GPU Sub-Cores
pb: Modern GPU sub-core partitioning reduces power and area but prevents task distribution across sub-cores; functional units (FUs) frequently stall waiting for results while adjacent sub-cores have unoccupied FUs, wasting compute capacity.
me: ACRS framework enables dynamic sharing of functional units among adjacent sub-cores through two modules: Shared FU Issue (SF_ISSUE) monitors operand collector and FU status, offloading stalled instructions to unoccupied FUs in adjacent sub-cores; Shared FU Write Back (SF_WriteBack) routes results back. Fixed target core assignment minimizes wiring overhead.
nv: First practical adjacent sub-core FU sharing mechanism for partitioned GPUs using dynamic instruction offloading and result routing.
th: Dynamic cross-sub-core functional unit sharing in partitioned GPUs

t: New Time-Domain Preconditioners for HB Jacobian of RF Circuits
pb: Harmonic balance (HB) Jacobian solving in RF circuit simulation requires efficient linear system solvers that balance computational cost with reduction in Newton iterations, especially for strongly nonlinear circuits.
me: Proposes novel time-domain preconditioners for HB Jacobian that address both linear solver efficiency and iteration step reduction. Extends preconditioning to distributed device circuits via a new approach. Introduces matrix norm-based nonlinearity metric for a priori preconditioner selection.
nv: First time-domain preconditioner design that balances linear solver efficiency with iteration reduction for nonlinear RF circuits.
th: Efficient preconditioners for RF circuit Jacobian solving

t: DAWN: Accelerating Point Cloud Object Detection via Object-Aware Partitioning and 3D Similarity-Based Filtering
pb: Point cloud object detection for autonomous driving and robotics faces high computational cost due to complex point processing on large per-frame point sets.
me: DAWN identifies frame-to-frame similarities and filters redundant points through object-aware partitioning based on previous detection results. Axis-sorted point selection refines partitioning for non-uniform point distributions. Efficient 3D similarity algorithm performs point filtering. Flexible latency-accuracy tradeoffs via configurable filtering ratios.
nv: Object-aware partitioning that leverages detection context to enable frame-based similarity filtering and redundancy elimination.
th: Frame-based point filtering for efficient 3D detection

t: Late Breaking Results: Advanced PCB Placement with Irregular Components for Efficient Collision Detection and Routability Optimization
pb: Automated PCB placement must handle heterogeneous components with irregular geometries and complex design rules while ensuring collision-free placement and routability.
me: Three-stage placement framework: (1) global placement with Separating Axis Theorem for collision detection on exact component contours and board shapes, (2) multi-stage force-directed method dynamically adjusting attractive/repulsive forces for clearance and routability, (3) scanline-based legalization resolving overlaps and enforcing spacing constraints. Framework adapts to diverse design limitations.
nv: Separating Axis Theorem-based collision detection for exact irregular component geometries in global PCB placement.
th: Collision-aware placement for irregular PCB components

t: LLMs Meet Post-Silicon Test Engineering: A New Era (Invited)
pb: Post-silicon test engineering requires domain-specific expertise; AI automation of test tasks is limited by lack of domain grounding.
me: Two-stage LLM-based AI agent framework for post-silicon test engineering: (1) reasoning stage interprets user queries using LLM capabilities, (2) grounding stage executes tasks by integrating LLM outputs with existing test infrastructure. Case study: Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) demonstrates autonomous task execution within established test framework.
nv: Domain-grounded LLM agents for post-silicon test automation, combining reasoning and infrastructure integration.
th: LLM-based agents for post-silicon test automation

t: Rank-based Multi-objective Approximate Logic Synthesis via Monte Carlo Tree Search
pb: Approximate logic synthesis focuses on single objectives (delay or area), leading to local optima in multi-objective optimization under error constraints.
me: Framework uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with non-dominated circuit ranking to guide exploration of local approximate changes (LACs). A Rank-Transformer model predicts path-domain ranks, enhancing high-quality LAC application.
nv: Non-dominated circuit ranking with MCTS to systematically explore the multi-objective approximate synthesis space.
th: Multi-objective approximate logic synthesis via Monte Carlo tree search

t: Truly Pre-Routing Timing Prediction via Considering Power Delivery Network
pb: Pre-routing timing prediction in chip design ignores power delivery network (PDN) effects, leading to inaccurate timing predictions. Existing ML-assisted methods fail to capture IR drop and routing congestion impacts on timing.
me: Proposes two specialized encoders—an IR drop-aware encoder and routing congestion-aware encoder—that fuse multimodal data (netlist, layout, PDN) through Pareto optimization to balance utilization across modalities for improved timing prediction accuracy on TSMC 16nm designs.
nv: Pareto optimization-based multimodal fusion that balances IR drop, routing congestion, and netlisting encoders to capture PDN effects in pre-routing timing.

mx.accuracy: improved over SOTA pre-routing timing methods

th: ML-assisted pre-routing timing with power delivery network awareness

t: DCDiff: Enhancing JPEG Compression via Diffusion-based DC Coefficients Estimation
pb: Low-cost cameras cannot support learning-based compressors; one approach drops DC coefficients at camera and reconstructs them later, but statistical reconstruction methods cause deviation-introduced errors that propagate throughout the image.
me: DCDiff uses a generative diffusion model to estimate DC coefficients end-to-end rather than relying on statistical methods. It generates masks to correct image locations violating statistical distributions, suppressing error propagation. The approach maintains full JPEG compatibility with typical low-cost processors.
nv: End-to-end generative diffusion model for DC coefficient reconstruction replaces statistical methods, avoiding error propagation and enabling learned priors for natural images.

mx.other: Outperforms baselines in compression performance; minimal downstream task impact (specific numbers not provided)

th: Diffusion model for JPEG DC coefficient reconstruction

t: 3D-Flow: Flow-based Standard Cell Legalization for 3D ICs
pb: Standard-cell placement legalization in 3D ICs must resolve overflows across multiple dies while minimizing cell displacement; traditional 2D legalizers are inefficient for 3D geometry.
me: Proposes 3D-Flow, a flow-based legalization algorithm that models the 3D space as a grid graph and finds shortest augmenting paths to resolve overflowed bins; uses branch-and-bound for path optimization and cycle-canceling post-optimization to minimize maximum displacement.
nv: Network flow formulation for 3D cell legalization leveraging global multi-die perspective to minimize displacement.

mx.other: 13% reduction in average cell displacement; 43% in maximum displacement

th: Network flow-based legalization for 3D IC placement

t: Late Breaking Results: Customized Diffusion Model Empowered by Heterogeneous Graph Network for Effective Floorplanning
pb: Classical analytical floorplanners are sensitive to initial solution quality; learning-based methods suffer high computational complexity and inefficiency.
me: Proposes a customized diffusion model generating high-quality initial floorplans; integrates heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) to capture block-to-block and pin-to-block relationships; introduces guidance sampling function optimizing wirelength and overlap.
nv: Diffusion model with HGNN feature extraction for initial floorplan generation, fed into analytical floorplanner.
th: Diffusion model with HGNN for initial floorplan generation

t: Curvilinear Optical Proximity Correction via Cardinal Spline
pb: Optical proximity correction (OPC) must handle curvilinear mask patterns with complex geometry; traditional OPC approaches struggle with curvature while maintaining mask rule checking compliance.
me: Proposes curvilinear OPC framework using cardinal splines to represent mask patterns through control points; iteratively adjusts control points guided by lithography simulation; develops comprehensive MRC checking methods for width, space, area, and curvature; designs algorithms to fit inverse lithography technique (ILT) results and resolve MRC violations.
nv: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear mask representation for OPC optimization with integrated MRC compliance.

mx.other: MRC compliance; pattern fidelity vs ILT results

th: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear OPC with MRC compliance

t: FactorHD: A Hyperdimensional Computing Model for Multi-Object Multi-Class Representation and Factorization
pb: Existing HDC models struggle to represent and factorize complex multi-object class-subclass relations; they suffer from superposition catastrophe and information loss when handling multiple objects simultaneously.
me: FactorHD encodes each object with a symbolic memorization clause to preserve multi-object information, avoiding superposition catastrophe. Factorization algorithm selectively eliminates redundant classes by identifying the memorization clause of the target class.
nv: Memorization-clause-based encoding enabling lossless factorization of multi-object class-subclass hierarchies in HDC.
th: Factorizable HDC

t: PatternPaint: Practical Layout Pattern Generation Using Diffusion-Based Inpainting
pb: VLSI layout pattern generation requires large, design-rule-compliant training datasets; new technology nodes lack such data, making existing training-based methods impractical.
me: PatternPaint uses diffusion-based inpainting with few-shot fine-tuning on pretrained image models; template-based denoising simplifies generation into inpainting tasks. Fine-tuning requires only 20 design-rule-compliant samples.
nv: Few-shot transfer learning via diffusion inpainting for layout pattern generation, eliminating need for large training corpora.
th: Few-shot layout generation

t: High Density Si-IPD Technologies as Enabler for High-Performance and Low-Power Consumption Processor Chips
pb: Power delivery networks in high-performance processors require large on-chip capacitance with minimal area footprint; traditional discrete capacitors consume significant board space. Si-IPD (Silicon Integrated Passive Devices) with high-density silicon capacitors integrate voltage regulation directly on-chip.
me: High-density Si-IPD technology integrates silicon capacitors and inductors directly into processor chips using specialized fabrication techniques, achieving higher capacitance density than traditional approaches and reducing parasitic resistance and inductance in the power delivery path.
nv: High-density integrated silicon passive devices enabling efficient on-chip power delivery with minimal area overhead.

mx.area: reduced board space for PDN components

th: Integrated silicon passive devices for power delivery

t: Specialized IC for World-Lock Rendering in Augmented and Mixed Reality Devices
pb: AR/MR requires real-time rendering of virtual objects locked to the physical world, demanding high-frequency pose tracking and low-latency graphics; this cannot be done efficiently on mobile CPUs.
me: The IC combines specialized vision (camera ISP, optical flow) and graphics engines optimized for tracking and rendering. It integrates pose estimation, world reconstruction, and graphics pipeline in silicon.
nv: Specialized IC architecture combining vision and graphics for real-time world-locked AR rendering on mobile form factors.
th: Specialized IC for real-time AR world-lock rendering

t: Hot ChipsKeynote
pb: Keynote presentation; no specific technical problem addressed.
me: Keynote address covering emerging trends and research opportunities.
nv: Vision for future directions in computing systems.
th: keynote address

t: R.I.P. Geomean Speedup Use Equal-Work (Or Equal-Time) Harmonic Mean Speedup Instead
pb: Geometric mean speedup, the dominant metric for summarizing multi-workload performance in computer architecture research, is mathematically ill-defined for speedup ratios and produces incorrect average speedup values that can lead to wrong architectural conclusions.
me: The paper derives the harmonic mean speedup from first principles under two explicit assumptions: equal-work (same total work executed on target and baseline, measuring how much faster the target finishes) and equal-time (same elapsed time, measuring how much more work is done). It demonstrates algebraically that equal-work harmonic mean correctly captures the aggregate speedup for a fixed workload mix, while the geometric mean does not. The paper further shows via concrete examples that geometric mean and harmonic mean can give opposite orderings of competing architectures.
nv: Formally establishing that equal-work harmonic mean speedup is the correct aggregate performance metric for computer architecture evaluation and providing a drop-in replacement methodology with clear semantics.
th: Correct statistical methodology for reporting aggregate speedup in computer architecture

t: CORDOBA: Carbon-Efficient Optimization Framework for Computing Systems
pb: Optimizing the carbon footprint of computing systems across large hardware design spaces is intractable with existing methods because it requires simultaneously trading off operational carbon, embodied carbon, performance, power, and area (PPA) under uncertainty in carbon intensity parameters.
me: CORDOBA introduces the total Carbon Delay Product (tCDP) metric — product of total lifecycle carbon (operational + embodied) and application execution time — as a single scalar objective for carbon-efficient hardware optimization. The framework performs design-space exploration by sweeping hardware configurations (e.g., core count, memory hierarchy, 2D vs. 3D integration via chiplet stacking) and evaluating tCDP under parametric uncertainty in carbon intensity, eliminating up to 98% of the design space as Pareto-dominated. Two case studies apply CORDOBA to real CPU systems: halving cores from 8 to 4 and adopting 3D-stacked logic+memory integration.
nv: The tCDP metric that jointly captures operational carbon, embodied carbon, and performance in one optimization target, enabling principled design-space pruning for carbon-efficient specialized hardware.

mx.other: tCDP improved 1.25x (8→4 cores); tCDP improved 6.9x (3D stacking vs. 2D); 98% design-space elimination

th: Carbon-aware hardware design-space optimization with lifecycle carbon metrics

t: Process Only Where You Look: Hardware and Algorithm Co-optimization for Efficient Gaze-Tracked Foveated Rendering in Virtual Reality
pb: Image rendering in VR head-mounted displays (HMDs) is computationally expensive, particularly for real-time applications where low latency is mandatory. Existing gaze-tracking and foveated rendering approaches impose high algorithmic and hardware costs that compound the overall rendering budget.
me: The paper proposes POLONet, an efficient multitask deep learning framework for real-time eye-movement tracking, co-designed with a dedicated POLO accelerator integrated as a plug-in for VR HMD SoCs. The system exploits the observation that human gaze is concentrated in a small foveal region, so full-resolution rendering is performed only where the eye is looking while peripheral regions are rendered at reduced quality. The hardware-algorithm co-optimization jointly minimizes gaze-tracking latency and rendering compute cost through a tightly coupled accelerator-SoC interface.
nv: A hardware-algorithm co-design that unifies multitask gaze tracking (POLONet) with a dedicated SoC accelerator (POLO) to achieve end-to-end foveated rendering with minimal latency overhead.

mx.speedup: 3.9x reduction in end-to-end latency vs. latest gaze tracking methods

th: gaze-driven foveated rendering accelerator

t: 15.1 A 3.9mW 200words/min Neural Signal Processor in Speech Decoding for Brain-Machine Interface
pb: Speech-based brain-machine interfaces require real-time neural network inference on implanted devices with ultra-low power budgets; existing high-end CPUs consume 65 W and require 5.3 seconds to decode a single word, making implantable BMI impractical.
me: A dedicated neural signal processor that maps the speech-decoding neural network (phone probability inference followed by beam-search word decoding using a language model) onto a specialized hardware pipeline. The design combines efficient NN inference blocks with language-model lookup acceleration to decode at 200 words/min.
nv: First dedicated hardware processor for speech-decoding BMI achieving real-time word-rate performance at implantable power levels (3.9 mW), demonstrating practical neural-network acceleration for biomedical inference.
th: Ultra-low-power speech-decoding neural accelerator for implantable BMI

t: 32.3 An Accurate Secondary-Side Controller with GaN-Based CGS Isolated Driver Achieving Sub-1% Error On-Chip Sensing
pb: LLC resonant converter secondary-side controllers require precise synchronous-rectifier (SR) on/off timing to minimize dead-time losses; conventional GaN SRs lack body diodes and suffer from current-collapse effects, and accurate current sensing at the secondary side is difficult to integrate.
me: A secondary-side controller with GaN-based common-gate-source (CGS) isolated driver enabling accurate on-chip current sensing via a gate-charge (CGS) monitoring technique. The driver provides strong driving capability with zero delay and precise SR timing while maintaining integrated current-sensing accuracy below 1% error.
nv: First demonstration of CGS-based isolated driver for GaN synchronous rectifiers with integrated sub-1% error current sensing, eliminating external sensing components and improving dead-time loss control.
th: Integrated GaN gate driver with sub-1% on-chip current sensing for efficient power conversion

t: 32.6 A Dynamic-RON-Diminished Bidirectional GaN Load Switch with Inrush Current Protection and Spike Attenuation
pb: Bidirectional GaN load switches for 48V EV power systems require both reverse-current blocking and bidirectional current transfer; monolithic bidirectional GaN (Bi-GaN) devices reduce on-resistance vs. discrete back-to-back solutions but suffer from overstress during turn-off when gate-to-source voltage exceeds breakdown limits, requiring complex turn-off selectors.
me: A dynamic-RON-diminished bidirectional GaN load switch using a monolithic bidirectional GaN device with CD (common-drain) topology. The design employs a novel turn-off control strategy that dynamically selects between gate-to-first-terminal or gate-to-second-terminal paths to avoid overstress, combined with inrush-current protection and spike-attenuation circuits.
nv: First monolithic Bi-GaN load switch with dynamic RON minimization and integrated overstress protection, achieving both efficient bidirectional switching and reliable gate-drive without complex external selectors.
th: Bidirectional GaN load switch with dynamic RON control for 48V EV power systems

t: 3.1 A 121.3dB-DR, 115dB-PSNR, Digital-Input Capacitive-Feedback Class-D Audio Amplifier with Double-Sided Voltage-Boosting (DSVB) Modulation
pb: Class-D audio amplifiers are limited in output power by battery voltage; prior approaches achieve boost via 2-stage DC-DC conversion (inefficient, ~80%) or single-stage buck-boost (limited dynamic range), struggling to combine high dynamic range (>120dB) with high efficiency and small form-factor.
me: Double-sided voltage-boosting (DSVB) modulation integrating capacitive-feedback chopper-amplifier with single-inductor buck-boost power stage, achieving high dynamic range (121.3dB DR) with 87% efficiency and only one off-chip inductor via single-stage power delivery.
nv: Single-inductor DSVB scheme combining capacitive-feedback noise elimination with buck-boost voltage boosting for simultaneous high DR and high efficiency.
th: Ultra-high-DR Class-D audio amplifier with single-inductor boost.

t: 34.2 A 380μW and -242.8dB FoM Digital-PLL-Based GFSK Modulator with Sub-20μs Settling Frequency Hopping for Bluetooth Low-Energy in 22nm CMOS
pb: Ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) transceivers must support GFSK modulation and adaptive frequency hopping (2.402-2.480GHz) with sub-20μs settling time while minimizing power dissipation, but existing DPLL-based approaches struggle with the power/noise/hopping-speed trade-off.
me: Digital-PLL-based GFSK modulator using dynamic-tuning-curve tracking and optimized DCO design to manage frequency modulation, hopping, and PVT variations with reduced switched-capacitor banks, achieving 380μW power at -242.8dB FoM with sub-20μs frequency hopping.
nv: Adaptive DCO switched-capacitor bank optimization reducing capacitive load while supporting fast frequency hopping via practical tuning-curve convergence.
th: Ultra-low-power DPLL-based BLE transceiver.

t: 20.11 A Crystal-Less BodyID with an Asynchronous Clockless Leakage-Powered Wake-Up Receiver and Over-the-Channel Clock Recovery
pb: Wake-up receivers for ultra-low-power wearables traditionally require always-running clocks and external crystal oscillators for sampling and correlation, consuming unnecessary idle power, adding size/cost, and requiring ULP oscillator with external calibration reference.
me: Asynchronous clockless wake-up receiver design leveraging over-the-channel clock recovery from incoming RF signal to enable direct digital correlation without always-running oscillator, powered by device leakage during idle state, eliminating need for external crystal reference.
nv: Clockless asynchronous design using in-band clock recovery to eliminate crystal oscillator and always-running clock, enabling full battery-less operation at leakage power levels.
th: Crystal-less asynchronous wake-up receiver.

t: A PVT-Robust 5.5GHz Fractional-N Cascaded RO-Based Digital PLL with Voltage-Domain Feedforward Noise Cancellation
pb: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based digital PLLs (DPLLs) offer compactness and immunity to magnetic coupling but suffer from high phase noise limited by quantization noise (Q-noise) and RO phase-noise (PN_RO). Prior PN-suppression techniques are prone to PVT variations, energy inefficient, or require complex correlation-based calibration of gain and threshold delays.
me: Fractional-N cascaded RO-DPLL using time-to-voltage converter (TVC) and ADC for PVT-robust Q-noise quantization, combined with voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation (V-FFNC) eliminating gain-calibration need, achieving 290.8fs rms jitter at 5.5GHz with <7.5% jitter deviation across PVT.
nv: Voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation enabling PVT-robust PN suppression without correlation-based gain calibration, reducing power and complexity.
th: PVT-robust RO-based fractional-N DPLL.

t: 5.5 An Ultra-Compact Wideband Load-Insensitive Complex-Cascode LC-Neutralized Power Amplifier for 4:1-VSWR-Resilient Operations in Large-Scale Phased Arrays
pb: Large-scale mm-wave phased arrays suffer from mutual antenna coupling causing antenna impedance variations across frequency, scanning angle (>60°), and array location, resulting in 4:1 voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) that degrades power amplifier (PA) output power, gain flatness, efficiency, and complicates array calibration.
me: Ultra-compact wideband PA using complex-cascode LC-neutralization topology achieving load-insensitive operation across 4:1 VSWR range, maintaining flat gain, OP1dB, and efficiency across frequency and scanning angle variations.
nv: LC-neutralized complex-cascode PA topology enabling VSWR resilience (4:1) without varactor tuning or switched-network impedance matching.
th: VSWR-resilient mm-wave PA for phased arrays.

t: 33.5 A 224GHz 19.9% TR Varactor-Less VCO Utilizing a Multi-Section Switch-Loaded Coupled-Line Resonator
pb: THz and sub-THz circuits require tunable elements like voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) and passive phase shifters, but varactors suffer from low Q-factor at frequencies >100GHz with limited tuning range, while switched-capacitor banks suffer from high OFF-state capacitance and low Q-factor.
me: 224GHz varactor-less VCO using multi-section switch-loaded coupled-line resonator achieving 19.9% tuning range through switched-inductor elements, overcoming varactor limitations and achieving high Q-factor at sub-THz frequencies.
nv: Multi-section switch-loaded coupled-line resonator design eliminating low-Q varactors while achieving >19% tuning range at sub-THz frequencies.
th: Sub-THz VCO via switch-loaded coupled-line.

t: 31.4 A 91.25% Peak Power-Conversion-Efficiency Capacitive Power-Management IC Supporting up to 5.68mJ Burst Energy Delivery Using a Single External Capacitor for mm-Scale IoT Applications
pb: mm-scale IoT devices with solid-state batteries face peak-power-delivery bottleneck due to high internal battery resistance (200Ω+), limiting burst energy to 4.8μJ, insufficient for peak transient loads (mW-level). Conventional approaches either use large storage capacitors (2% energy extraction) or on-chip capacitors (limited density at 0.87nJ), leaving most stored energy unutilized.
me: Capacitive power-management IC using single external storage capacitor charged to high voltage, continuously stepped up/down via on-chip switched-capacitor (SC) converter during burst mode, achieving 91.25% energy-extraction efficiency delivering up to 5.68mJ (40x improvement over prior on-chip approaches).
nv: Single-capacitor high-voltage pre-charging strategy with on-chip step-up/-down SC converter enabling >35x burst-energy-delivery improvement vs. prior methods.
th: Efficient burst-energy delivery via capacitive power management.

t: 5.10 A 3.5mW mm-Wave Low-Noise Active Bandpass Filter Employing an All-Passive Interferer-Cancellation Feedforward Path
pb: Millimeter-wave receivers require simultaneous low-noise, high-linearity, and sharp filtering to reject out-of-band interferers, but existing architectures (N-path filters, IF filtering, passive front-end) trade off noise, linearity, or filtering performance.
me: An LNA with an all-passive interferer-cancellation feedforward path pre-filters signals before experiencing device nonlinearities, enabling sharp filter shapes via cancellation-based techniques while maintaining low noise and high linearity.
nv: All-passive feedforward cancellation path integrated within LNA for simultaneous low-noise and high-linearity filtering without significant power overhead.
th: All-passive mm-wave LNA with integrated interferer-cancellation filter

t: 34.3 A 4.75GHz Digital PLL with 45.8fs Integrated-Jitter and 257dB FoM Based on a Voltage-Biased Harmonic-Shaping DCO with Adaptive Common-Mode Resonance Tuning
pb: Digital PLLs for low-jitter synthesis must minimize DCO flicker and white noise, but voltage-biased DCOs require complex tuning-bank segmentation and extensive manual common-mode (CM) resonance tuning that is PVT-sensitive.
me: A voltage-biased DCO with harmonic-shaping architecture employs adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, enabling automatic foreground/background tuning across PVT variations. The approach uses wideband CM resonance expansion via transformer to maintain high CM impedance across the full tuning range.
nv: Automatic adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, eliminating manual tuning complexity and improving PVT robustness.
th: Voltage-biased DCO with automatic adaptive common-mode resonance tuning for low-jitter PLL

t: 18.3: A 93.3dB SNDR, 180.4dB FoMs Calibration-Free Noise-Shaping Pipelined-SAR ADC with Cross-Stage Gain-Mismatch-Error-Shaping Technique and Negative-R-Assisted Residue Integrator
pb: High-resolution pipelined-SAR ADCs suffer from mismatch errors and inter-stage gain errors; prior gain-error-shaping (GES) schemes introduce multi-bit feedback with additional mismatch sources (truncation and quantization noise) requiring extensive calibration.
me: A calibration-free pipelined-SAR ADC uses cross-stage gain-mismatch-error-shaping that directly combines GES and MES without multi-bit feedback, leveraging a negative-resistance-assisted residue integrator to enable efficient analog integration and error shaping.
nv: Cross-stage gain-mismatch-error-shaping technique enabling single-bit feedback combination of GES and MES without auxiliary mismatch contributors.
th: Calibration-free pipelined-SAR ADC with unified cross-stage gain-mismatch error shaping

t: A Single-Inductor-Based High-Voltage Transmit Beamformer for Wearable Ultrasound Devices Achieving 88% fCV2 Power Reduction
pb: Wearable ultrasound transducer arrays for vagus nerve stimulation suffer from excessive power loss from charging/discharging transducer capacitance (fCV² loss); prior resonant pulsers require multiple off-chip inductors, incompatible with miniaturized form factors.
me: A single-inductor resonant transmit beamformer architecture pulses groups of transducer elements at different phases from a shared inductor, enabling energy recycling across the array while avoiding the complex body-diode losses of prior approaches.
nv: Single-inductor architecture enabling efficient TX beamforming through phase-shifted pulsing of element groups, eliminating multiple off-chip inductors while maintaining resonant energy recycling.

mx.power_reduction: 88% fCV² loss reduction vs. class-D pulser

th: Single-inductor resonant TX beamformer for wearable ultrasound therapy

t: 34.4 A 9.05-to-37.0GHz LO Generator with Magnetic Mode Switching and Tuning-Free Octave-Bandwidth Common-Mode Resonator Achieving >190.7dBc/Hz FoM
pb: VCOs with octave-plus tuning range (>10GHz center frequency) face challenges maintaining low phase noise while spanning wide frequency coverage; multi-core multi-mode architectures are complex and require extensive tuning.
me: An octave-bandwidth VCO uses magnetic mode switching to transition between operating bands and implements a tuning-free common-mode resonator with automatic frequency tracking across the full tuning range, eliminating manual mode transitions.
nv: Automatic magnetic-mode-switching architecture with tuning-free octave-bandwidth common-mode resonator eliminating complex mode manual control.
th: Automatic magnetic-mode VCO with tuning-free octave-bandwidth resonator

t: 21.7 Merging Hybrid and Multi-Phase Topologies: A 6-Phase Triple-Step-Down DC-DC Converter Achieving up to a 60:1 Voltage Conversion Ratio and 868A/cm3 Current Density
pb: Modern processors require efficient point-of-load DC-DC converters delivering high current (>1A) at extreme voltage step-down (12V to <1V); conventional single-phase buck struggles with large step-down/current, hybrid converters scale poorly with current (flying capacitors), and multi-phase designs require more inductor inductance.
me: A 6-phase triple-step-down hybrid-multi-phase architecture combines the inductance advantages of multi-phase designs with flying-capacitor efficiency of hybrid topologies. Instead of scaling flying capacitors, the design exploits multiple compact inductors, achieving lower total volume and higher current density with reduced DCR.
nv: Hybrid-multi-phase merger that balances inductive step-down across phases while using flying capacitors only where beneficial, enabling 868A/cm³ current density.
th: 6-phase hybrid-multi-phase DC-DC converter for extreme voltage step-down and high current density

t: A Dual-Input Bidirectional 3-Level Battery Charger with Coarse-Fine VCF Balancing and Wide VCR for Foldable Mobile Applications
pb: Foldable mobile phones require high-density battery charging with compact passive components and support for simultaneous wired and wireless charging plus wireless power sharing (reverse direction). Existing 2-level converters suffer from size/efficiency tradeoffs.
me: A bidirectional 3-level topology with dual input switches (D_CHG for wired, D_wc for wireless) seamlessly transitions between buck charging, boost reverse-feed (when battery powers external load), and idle modes. Coarse-fine voltage-controlled-frequency (VCF) balancing maintains stable inductor current across modes; wide voltage-conversion-ratio (VCR) coverage eliminates need for separate low/high-band RF chains.
nv: Seamless mode transition between buck and reverse-boost operations without auxiliary circuits, enabled by coordinated multi-level switching and adaptive frequency control.

mx.other: Seamless mode transition, wide input range support

th: Bidirectional multi-level charging for foldable phones

t: 15.4 A Neuroprosthetic SoC with Sensory Feedback Featuring Frequency-Splitting-Based Wireless Power Transfer with 200Mb/s 0.67pJ/b Backscatter Data Uplink and Unsupervised Multi-Class Spike Sorting
pb: High-channel neural implants enable prosthetic control but lack closed-loop sensory feedback, limiting stability and requiring steep user learning curves. Traditional external feedback introduces latency; electrical stimulation is viable but must reject stimulation artifacts to avoid false feedback loops.
me: Frequency-splitting wireless power transfer delivers power and data on distinct carriers, eliminating cross-talk. Backscatter uplink (200 Mb/s, 0.67 pJ/bit) conveys neural data with minimal power overhead. On-chip unsupervised multi-class spike sorting classifies neural signals locally, reducing data bandwidth. Stimulation artifact rejection circuit prevents positive feedback loops during simultaneous stimulation and recording.
nv: Frequency-splitting WPT + backscatter uplink enables simultaneous power delivery and high-speed data transmission without cross-interference, reducing implant battery size.
th: Implantable prosthetic SoC with closed-loop feedback

t: 21.9 A 20MHz & 1MHz Dual-Loop Non-Uniform-Multi-Inductor Hybrid DC-DC Converter with Specified Inductor Current Allocation and Fast Transient Response
pb: Series-capacitor buck (SCB) hybrid converters offer efficiency but suffer from slow load transient response due to low loop bandwidth (1/10–1/5 of switching frequency) and inability to rapidly increase inductor current slew rate during transients. Multiple inductors cannot simultaneously activate; load step-down slew rate limited by low V_out and large inductance.
me: Dual-loop control (20 MHz outer loop + 1 MHz inner loop) and non-uniform multi-inductor architecture enable concurrent inductor activation during load steps. Specified current allocation strategy distributes transient current among inductors optimally. Direct control of per-inductor current slew rates through selective switch timing improves load step response dynamics without sacrificing efficiency.
nv: Non-uniform multi-inductor SC buck with dual-loop control and specified current allocation achieves 2x faster load step response vs. single-loop designs while maintaining SCB efficiency benefits.

mx.other: 2x load step slew rate improvement, fast transient response

th: Fast transient multi-inductor buck hybrid DC-DC

t: 32.4 A Dual-LC-Resonant Isolated DC-DC Converter Achieving 65.4% Peak Efficiency and Inherent Backscattering
pb: Integrated isolated DC-DC converters (with on-chip transformers) suffer from low peak efficiency (~52%) due to TX LC-oscillator losses, RX full-bridge rectifier losses, and parasitic transformer elements. Traditional feedback from RX to TX requires costly digital isolators; alternative RX-only regulation approaches sacrifice efficiency (<37%).
me: Dual-LC-resonant topology optimizes TX and RX resonators independently. TX uses optimized LC oscillator; RX employs resonant rectification (not full-bridge) to reduce rectifier losses. Inherent backscattering mechanism enables RX-to-TX feedback via modulating load impedance on resonator, eliminating need for digital isolator while maintaining RX-side regulation.
nv: Dual-LC resonant topology with inherent backscatter feedback achieves 65.4% peak efficiency while eliminating digital isolators—a 6–13% efficiency gain over state-of-the-art.
th: Dual-LC resonant isolated DC-DC with backscatter

t: 19.3 A Fractional-N PLL with 34fsrms Jitter and -255.5dB FoM Based on a Multipath Feedback Technique
pb: Advanced wireless communication (4K-QAM and beyond) requires frequency synthesizers with sub-100 fs RMS jitter to meet stringent phase-noise requirements. Prior fractional-N PLLs achieve excellent jitter but rely on impractically high reference frequencies (150–500 MHz), unsuitable for cost-effective deployment.
me: Multipath feedback technique in an analog PLL architecture enables competitive jitter performance despite low 80 MHz reference frequency (7.5x lower than prior sub-100 fs designs). The technique exploits parallel feedback paths to reduce charge-pump dead-zone and reference spur injection, improving phase margin and jitter. PLL operates 7.3–9.5 GHz output range.
nv: Multipath feedback technique in analog PLL achieves 34 fs RMS jitter at practical 80 MHz reference frequency, eliminating need for expensive high-frequency references.

mx.other: Jitter 34 fs RMS, FoM -255.5 dB, frequency range 7.3–9.5 GHz

th: Low-reference-freq PLL for cost-effective wireless

t: 4.2 A 1.8-to-3.0GHz Fully Integrated All-In-One CMOS Frequency Management Module Achieving -47/+42ppm Inaccuracy from -40 to 95°C and -150/+70ppm After Accelerated Aging
pb: Wireless/wired communication systems require stable frequency references, traditionally using bulky off-chip crystals. On-chip RC-based references struggle with poor aging performance (>±1030 ppm drift after aging even with redundancy) and inadequate frequency accuracy for modern protocols; integrating on-chip reference into synthesizer for true FMM remains unachieved.
me: Fully integrated frequency management module (FMM) combines on-chip frequency reference (RC-based with improved stability techniques) and frequency synthesizer in single CMOS chip. Covers 1.8–3.0 GHz output range; achieves ±47/±42 ppm inaccuracy across -40 to +95°C (far superior to prior RC-core designs). Post-aging specs: ±150/±70 ppm after accelerated testing.
nv: First integration of fully on-chip RC reference with synthesizer achieving frequency-management specs comparable to crystal alternatives, eliminating off-chip frequency trim.
th: Crystal-free fully integrated frequency management

t: 9.11 A 98.3%-Peak-Efficiency Single-Mode Hybrid Buck-Boost Converter with 7mV Maximum Output Ripple for Li-Ion Battery Management
pb: Conventional hybrid buck-boost converters with multiple modes suffer from voltage glitches and output overshoot during transitions; single-mode cascaded designs trade efficiency for mode-transition robustness, suffering from reduced efficiency and large output ripple due to discontinuous current delivery.
me: Single-mode topology cascading a boost and buck bridge using a flying capacitor to reduce switch voltage stress and enable continuous current delivery across operating range, eliminating mode-transition issues and output ripple.
nv: Single-mode cascaded buck-boost topology with continuous current delivery eliminating mode transitions and their associated voltage stress/ripple.
th: High-efficiency continuous-current buck-boost for battery systems

t: 6.5 A 25.2Mpixel 120frames/s Full-Frame Global-Shutter CMOS Image Sensor with Pixel-Parallel ADC
pb: Conventional rolling-shutter sensors have image distortion, flicker effects, and flash bands; previous global-shutter approaches (charge-domain, voltage-domain) fail to meet consumer ILC camera requirements for dynamic range and random noise; scaling pixel-parallel ADCs to tens of megapixels while maintaining image quality and low power consumption is challenging.
me: 25.2Mpixel 120fps full-frame sensor using pixel-parallel ADC in stacked structure, achieving global shutter with high dynamic range and low random noise by distributing ADC processing at pixel level.
nv: Stacked pixel-parallel ADC architecture scaling to 25Mpixel for global-shutter high-DR operation.
th: Megapixel global-shutter sensor with pixel-parallel ADC

t: A Programming-Free Three-Dimensional Resonant Current-Mode Wireless Receiver with Real-Time Link-Adaptivity and a 0.904cm3 Receiver Coil for Implantable Systems
pb: Wireless power transfer (WPT) for implantable medical devices (IMDs) must balance high efficiency, small form factor, tissue safety (heating, EM field exposure), and surgical practicality while enabling wireless charging without infection risk.
me: A resonant current-mode (RCM) WPT receiver with real-time link-adaptivity uses a 3D receiver coil (0.904cm³) for compact integration, autonomous tuning to tissue impedance variations, and low-power capability without programming overhead.
nv: Programming-free real-time link-adaptivity in RCM WPT with compact 3D coil integration for implantable systems.
th: Compact adaptive wireless power for implantable devices

t: A Biased-SECE Interface for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting with Geometric-Mean-Computational MPPT Achieving 99.9% MPPT Efficiency, 8.75Cycles/ΔVOC Tracking, and 9.3x Energy Extraction
pb: Piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH) systems must achieve accurate and responsive maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking; fractional open-circuit voltage (FOCV) causes energy interruption, while perturb-and-observe (P&O) and duty-cycle methods trade off tracking speed vs accuracy.
me: A biased-SECE (switch-harvesting-on-inductor-peak (SHIP) with parallel SECE) interface uses geometric-mean-computational MPPT that avoids discontinuities in energy extraction, achieves fast online tracking of open-circuit voltage (8.75 cycles/ΔV_OC), and delivers 99.9% MPPT efficiency.
nv: Geometric-mean-computational MPPT scheme enabling continuous energy extraction with sub-cycle-level tracking responsiveness without energy interruptions.
th: Geometric-mean MPPT for continuous fast-tracking piezoelectric energy harvesting

t: 5.4 A 22nm FDSOI CMOS-Based Compact 3-Stack Doherty Power Amplifier with a Stacked OPA-Based Bias Scheme Achieving >16.5dBm Pavg for 5G FR2 Applications
pb: Power amplifiers in 5G phased-array systems must deliver high output power (>70dBm EIRP) while maintaining efficiency during signal back-off (>10dB PAPR), necessitating compact, highly integrated designs in silicon CMOS.
me: The design employs a compact 3-stack Doherty PA structure in 22nm FDSOI CMOS with a stacked OPA-based bias scheme. The Doherty topology dynamically modulates the peak/auxiliary amplifier impedance to maintain high PAE across a wide power range, while the stacked OPA bias improves efficiency at back-off conditions.
nv: Stacked OPA-based bias scheme enabling high efficiency in compact 3-stack Doherty architecture for mm-wave integration.
th: Efficient compact Doherty power amplifier for 5G mm-wave phased arrays

t: A 97.4%-Peak-Efficiency Always-Half-Inductor-Current Hybrid Bidirectional Converter With Adaptive Target Current Tracking for USB-to-2-Cell Bidirectional Power Transfer
pb: Bidirectional DC-DC converters for 2-cell batteries (6-8.4V) suffer from high inductor DC resistance losses and require expensive high-voltage transistors, limiting efficiency in both forward (USB charging) and on-the-go (OTG power delivery) modes.
me: The design uses an always-half-inductor-current hybrid converter topology that reduces peak inductor current by half compared to conventional boost/buck topologies, thereby minimizing DCR losses. Adaptive target current tracking dynamically optimizes operating point across loading conditions. The hybrid approach operates as a boost in forward mode and buck in OTG mode with reduced inductor stress.
nv: Always-half-inductor-current hybrid topology with adaptive target current tracking achieving peak efficiency while reducing inductor and transistor stress.
th: High-efficiency hybrid bidirectional converter for portable device battery management

t: 11.5 A 200MHz-BW Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with Fifth-Order Filtering Achieving 19dBm Adjacent-Channel IIP3
pb: 5G NR receivers with 200+ MHz channel bandwidth must handle strong in-band and adjacent-channel blockers while maintaining low noise figure and acceptable power consumption, requiring aggressive analog filtering before digitization.
me: The receiver employs a fifth-order filtering architecture, likely using mixer-first topology with baseband input impedance (Z_BB) exhibiting steep roll-off greater than 20dB/dec. This provides sharp nearby filtering at the RX input while maintaining passive gain through capacitor stacking, carefully trading off noise figure against power consumption.
nv: Fifth-order filtering architecture achieving steep blocker suppression with improved power efficiency compared to prior mixer-first approaches.
th: High-order filtering receiver for 5G blocker-tolerant wideband reception

t: 19.7 A 27GHz Fractional-N Sub-Sampling PLL Achieving 57.9fsrms Jitter, -249.7dB FoM, and 1.98µS Locking Time Using Polarity-Reversible SSPD
pb: Mm-wave fractional-N PLLs with sub-100fs jitter face challenges in DTC range reduction at high frequencies where prescalers enlarge DTC range, and suffer from prolonged locking times in sub-sampling PLLs due to small SSPD capture range.
me: The fractional-N sub-sampling PLL (SSPLL) employs a polarity-reversible SSPD (phase detector) that samples both rising and falling edges of the oscillator output, reducing DTC range without requiring prescalers. A low-power TDC-based frequency-locked loop (FLL) enables fast locking in fractional mode by compensating the frequency error beyond ref_clock frequency limits, achieving sub-microsecond locking time.
nv: Polarity-reversible SSPD enabling reduced DTC range without prescalers; TDC-based FLL enabling fast fractional locking.
th: Ultra-low jitter fractional-N mm-wave PLL with fast locking via polarity-reversible SSPD

t: A 185.2dB-FoMs 8.7aFrms Zoomed Capacitance-to-Digital Converter with Chopping-Based kT/C Noise Cancellation and Add-Then-Subtract Phase-Domain Lead-Compensation Technique
pb: VCO-based time-domain delta-sigma capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) face kT/C sampling noise exacerbation at reduced oversampling ratios and lack efficient feedforward compensation techniques for VCO's intrinsically fused integrator and quantizer.
me: The zoom CDC architecture combines SAR coarse stage with VCO-based time-domain fine stage. It employs: (1) chopping-based kT/C noise cancellation requiring only minimal amplification (vs. conventional methods needing power-hungry amplifiers); (2) add-then-subtract phase-domain lead-compensation technique enabling stable high-order loop without linearity penalties; (3) VCO's intrinsic phase integration obviated the need for OTAs.
nv: Chopping-based kT/C cancellation with efficient phase-domain lead-compensation enabling high-order VCO delta-sigma without OTA overhead.
th: Ultra-low-noise zoomed capacitance-to-digital converter with chopping and phase-domain compensation

t: 4.6 A 0.8V, 31ppm/°C, -40dB DC-to-GHz Power-Supply-Rejection Standard-Vth Core-MOS-Only Voltage Reference with a 294µm2Area
pb: PVT-independent voltage references at sub-1V core-supply operation face headroom limitations from BJT V_EB and current-source saturation voltage; existing approaches require DNW base structures (non-standard CMOS) or switching-mode ripple filters (large area).
me: A standard-Vth core-MOS-only voltage reference operating at 0.8V uses charge-pump or switched-capacitor techniques to reduce supply headroom requirements beyond traditional BJT approaches. Achieves 31ppm/°C temperature coefficient with -40dB power-supply-rejection ratio (PSRR) across DC-to-GHz frequencies. Compact design uses only core devices without DNW structures.
nv: Standard-Vth MOS-only reference achieving 0.8V operation with excellent PSRR and minimal area using charge-pump/switched-capacitor techniques.
th: Ultra-compact sub-1V core-MOS voltage reference with high PSRR

t: 2.8: A 210fps Image Signal Processor for 4K Ultra HD True Video Super Resolution
pb: Conventional video super-resolution treats frames as independent images, neglecting temporal and spatial redundancies in video encoding (I/P/B frames, block prediction, residuals), resulting in inefficient computation and high energy cost.
me: A dedicated video super-resolution ISP leverages inter-frame dependencies and video codec structure. The processor exploits temporal redundancy by reusing features from adjacent frames and spatial redundancy by utilizing residual/motion vector information from codec blocks. Multi-frame alignment and refinement stages process P/B frames referencing previous/future frames, incorporating motion vectors and residuals directly into the VSR pipeline rather than treating video as raw frames.
nv: Video-codec-aware super-resolution ISP exploiting temporal/spatial redundancies in frame encoding to achieve high throughput with low energy.
th: Codec-aware 4K video super-resolution ISP exploiting temporal/spatial redundancy

t: A 132-to-148GHz CMOS 4TX-4RX FMCW Radar Transceiver Array with Cavity-Backed Antenna-in-Package Achieving 28dBm EIRP
pb: D-band (132-148GHz) FMCW radar transceivers are limited by low output power from frequency multipliers and power amplifiers, low on-chip antenna gain, and small array sizes, resulting in insufficient EIRP (<11.6 dBm) for high-resolution imaging and long-range detection.
me: The transceiver array implements four transmit and four receive channels with a high-power amplitude-phase harmonic modulated frequency quadrupler, high-power PA using low-loss slow-wave coplanar waveguide (CPW) and LC-ladder-based power-combiner, and a cavity-backed antenna-in-package (AiP) with high gain to achieve 28.7 dBm EIRP.
nv: Cavity-backed antenna-in-package integration combined with LC-ladder power-combiner achieving unprecedented D-band EIRP for multi-channel FMCW radar arrays.
th: High-EIRP D-band FMCW radar transceiver array

t: 13.1 A 0.22mm2 161nW Noise-Robust Voice-Activity Detection Using Information-Aware Data Compression and Neuromorphic Spatial-Temporal Feature Extraction
pb: Always-on voice-activity detection (VAD) dominates power consumption in voice processing systems; achieving ultra-low power consumption (<200nW) while maintaining noise robustness (0-5dB SNR) and high accuracy (>90%) without excessive spike generation from feature encoding is challenging.
me: The 161nW VAD engine combines information-aware data compression for efficient feature encoding with neuromorphic spatial-temporal feature extraction using spiking neural networks (SNNs) that reduce spike generation compared to level-crossing coding methods.
nv: Information-aware data compression combined with neuromorphic spatial-temporal feature extraction achieving ultra-low power VAD with maintained noise robustness.
th: Ultra-low-power neuromorphic voice-activity detection

t: A 0.4µW/MHz Reference-Replication-Based RC Oscillator with Path-Delay and Comparator-Offset Cancellation Achieving 9.83ppm/°C from -40 to 125°C
pb: Open-loop RC oscillators struggle with frequency stability against process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations due to path-delay and comparator offset sensitivity; closed-loop approaches achieve better stability but incur significant area, power, and circuit complexity overhead.
me: The reference-replication-based RC oscillator cancels path-delay and comparator-offset effects through integrated compensation circuits, achieving ±9.83ppm/°C temperature coefficient across -40 to 125°C while maintaining 0.4µW/MHz power efficiency without switched resistors or polynomial calibration.
nv: Integrated path-delay and comparator-offset cancellation in open-loop RC oscillators eliminating the complexity-stability tradeoff of prior designs.
th: Stable low-power RC oscillator for IoT timing

t: 19.10 A 4.6GHz 63.3fsrms PLL-XO Co-Design Using a Self-Aligned Pulse-Injection Driver Achieving -255.2dB FoMJ Including the XO Power and Noise
pb: Phase-locked loop (PLL) jitter and power optimization historically neglects the full frequency-generation chain including crystal oscillator (XO) driver, reference buffer, and PLL itself, resulting in suboptimal overall system jitter figure-of-merit.
me: The PLL-XO co-design employs a self-aligned pulse-injection driver that optimizes the interaction between crystal oscillator and PLL, achieving 4.6GHz operation with 63.3fs integrated jitter while including XO power and noise in a unified -255.2dB figure-of-merit.
nv: Self-aligned pulse-injection driver enabling co-design optimization of PLL and crystal oscillator for improved jitter figure-of-merit including full system power and noise.
th: Low-jitter PLL with crystal oscillator co-design

t: 18.2 A 12.2µW 99.6dB-SNDR 184.8dB-FOMs DT Zoom PPD ΔΣM with Gain-Embedded Bootstrapped Sampler
pb: Discrete-time (DT) delta-sigma modulators require large sampling capacitors to achieve high resolution, imposing huge driving burden on input buffers to settle charges; the input driver dominates power consumption while most current is wasted through passive components.
me: The 12.2µW DT zoom PPD ΔΣM employs a gain-embedded bootstrapped sampler that integrates gain into the sampling stage, reducing settling requirements and input buffer current demands while maintaining high linearity and SNDR performance.
nv: Gain-embedded bootstrapped sampler architecture reducing input-stage power consumption in high-resolution DT ΔΣMs.
th: Ultra-low-power high-resolution delta-sigma ADC

t: 5.1 A GaN SLCG-Doherty-Continuum Power Amplifier Achieving >38% 6dB Back-Off Efficiency Over 1.35 to 7.6GHz
pb: Wireless systems with hundreds of MHz bandwidth and complex modulations (high PAPR) require power amplifiers with large RF bandwidth, high back-off efficiency, good linearity, and compact size; gallium nitride (GaN) technology offers high power density but efficiency degrades significantly at back-off.
me: The GaN power amplifier implements a series-load conducting Gallium Nitride (SLCG) combined with Doherty-Continuum architecture to achieve high efficiency across wide frequencies (1.35-7.6GHz) and power back-off conditions.
nv: SLCG-Doherty-Continuum architecture enabling >38% efficiency at 6dB back-off over multi-octave frequency range.
th: Wideband GaN power amplifier with high back-off efficiency

t: 26.1: A 24GHz Direct Digital Transmitter Using Multiphase Subharmonic Switching PA Achieving 3.2Gb/s Data Rate and -30.8dB EVM in 65nm CMOS
pb: Wide-bandwidth (multi-Gb/s) RF transmitters for K/Ka-band (24GHz) must achieve low EVM and high efficiency across peak and back-off power levels, but IQ summation causes 3dB power loss and prior subharmonic switching (SHS) designs were bandwidth-limited to tens of MHz.
me: Multiphase subharmonic switching (MP-SHS) transmitter architecture combines phase-shifted subharmonic LO divider (attenuating subharmonic spurs via phase shift), current-shared phase-interpolator MUX for MP LO generation, and dual-rate hybrid DAC with noise shaping to enable 3.2Gb/s operation at 24GHz while maintaining peak and PBO efficiency.
nv: Multiphase SHS architecture mitigates both the 3dB IQ power loss and low PBO efficiency of prior approaches by distributing power across multiple phases while using phase-shifted subharmonic LO dividers to suppress spurs.

mx.speedup: 3.2 Gb/s data rate (vs. tens of MHz in prior SHS work)

th: Multiphase subharmonic switching for high-efficiency wideband RF transmission

t: A 10.5mW Automotive Touch AFE IC Featuring Radiated EMI Reduction Based on Pipelined Dual-Frequency Modulation and Sine2 Waveform Shaping for CISPR 25 Class 5 Compliance
pb: Automotive touch-screen sensors must comply with CISPR 25 EMI standards while maintaining high SNR and frame rate, but typical driving signals (200-500kHz) radiate harmonics that violate emission limits; prior approaches (COM, high-voltage, PRP, FDM) either require FFT overhead or are ineffective at attenuating harmonics.
me: Pipelined dual-frequency modulation combined with sine2 waveform shaping in the AFE to reduce radiated EMI without FFT overhead; selective driving signal modulation attenuates harmonics while maintaining SNR and frame rate performance.
nv: Sine2 waveform shaping combined with pipelined dual-frequency modulation achieves CISPR 25 compliance without FFT-based filtering, eliminating area and power overhead of traditional FDM approaches.

mx.other: CISPR 25 Class 5 EMI compliance, maintained SNR and frame rate

th: EMI-compliant automotive touch AFE via optimized waveform shaping

t: 27.2 A Voltage-Biased CMOS Hall Sensor with 1.0sµT(3σ) Offset and a 60nT/√Hz Noise-Floor
pb: Traditional current-biased Hall sensors exhibit large offset errors (tens of µT), limiting their use in precision applications like compasses and current sensors; voltage-biased architectures may offer lower offset but require novel readout design.
me: Voltage-biased Hall sensor (vs. traditional current-bias) with low-offset readout circuit in standard 0.18µm CMOS; dual arrangement outputs current rather than voltage, enabling offset cancellation and noise reduction through custom frontend design.
nv: Voltage-biased Hall sensor topology with optimized readout achieves 3x lower offset (1.0µT) and 5x better noise floor (60nT/√Hz) compared to prior current-biased approaches, demonstrating architectural shift improves DC magnetic sensing.

mx.other: 3x offset reduction, 5x noise improvement vs prior art

th: Low-offset voltage-biased CMOS Hall sensor

t: 5.8 A 20W CMOS/LDMOS All-Digital Transmitter with Dynamic Retiming and Glitch-Free Phase Mapper, Achieving 68%/62% Peak Drain/System Efficiency
pb: Base stations dominate wireless operator energy consumption (73%); analog PA-based transmitters suffer from high quiescent currents and limited bandwidth, but achieving high-power all-digital transmitters (DTX) at mMIMO levels (>3W) requires fine gate segmentation and glitch-free operation for wideband modulation.
me: 8-phase multi-phase digital upconversion transmitter with dynamic retiming and glitch-free phase-mapper; custom low-VT LDMOS MMIC with power switch banks featuring in-finger gate segmentation and high-density flip-chip DTX controller integration.
nv: First all-digital transmitter achieving mMIMO power levels (20W integrated) with wideband modulation support through dynamic retiming and glitch-free phase mapping, demonstrating DTX viability for base-station deployment.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: 68% peak drain efficiency, 62% peak system efficiency

th: High-power all-digital transmitter for energy-efficient base stations

t: 20.1 A 3.5×3.5mm2 1.47mW/ch 16-Channel MSS-CMOS Heterogeneous Multi-Modal-Gas-Sensor Chip Stack
pb: Miniaturized multi-channel gas sensors with low power are needed for wearables, ingestible biomedical devices, and smart tags, but traditional gas sensors separate transducers from CMOS via wiring, requiring large packaging; prior MEMS-CMOS stacks lack multi-gas capability and scalability.
me: Heterogeneous MEMS-CMOS stack integrating Membrane-type Surface-stress Sensor (MSS) transducers on top of CMOS analog frontend and digital readout; 16-channel architecture with 1.47mW/channel power on 3.5×3.5mm2 footprint.
nv: First demonstration of multi-modal gas sensing via MSS-CMOS heterogeneous stack at 16-channel density, proving compact form factor and low per-channel power enable deployment in wearables and ingestible devices.
th: Compact heterogeneous multi-modal gas sensor stack

t: 9.8 A 50W 98%-Efficiency High-Power Wireless-Charging System with an Acoustic Noise-Reduced Ask Modulation Technique and Internal Hybrid Voltage-/Current-Mode ASK Demodulation
pb: High-power wireless charging (Qi MPP >25W) requires frequent and accurate transmitter-receiver (TRX) communication for safety and signal quality, but ASK modulation can introduce acoustic noise in receiver coil; traditional demodulation approaches are inefficient.
me: 50W Qi wireless power transfer system with acoustic noise-reduced ASK modulation in transmitter and hybrid voltage-/current-mode ASK demodulation in receiver; achieves 98% efficiency with improved communication reliability.
nv: Acoustic noise-reduced ASK modulation combined with hybrid voltage-/current-mode receiver demodulation enables high-power Qi 2.0 compliance at 98% efficiency while eliminating coil acoustic artifacts.
th: High-efficiency Qi wireless charging with acoustic noise control

t: 19.6 A 60GHz I/Q-Calibrated SSB-Mixer-Based LO with Sub-ns Settling Time and -56dBc Worst-Case Spur Using ILO Filter in 28nm CMOS
pb: Joint Communication-and-Sensing (JCAS) systems using SC-OFDM (stepped-carrier OFDM) require local oscillators (LOs) with fast frequency-hopping settling (<18ns for IEEE 802.11ay) and low spurious tones; traditional LOs cannot meet both stringent jitter and settling requirements simultaneously.
me: 60GHz SSB (single-sideband) mixer-based LO with integrated LC oscillator (ILO) filter; achieves sub-ns settling via rapid frequency-hop architecture and I/Q calibration to suppress spurs to -56dBc worst-case.
nv: First SSB-mixer-based LO with ILO filter achieving sub-nanosecond settling for mmWave SC-OFDM JCAS, demonstrating that fast frequency hopping is compatible with low-spur performance through ILO filtering and I/Q calibration.

mx.other: Sub-nanosecond settling time, -56 dBc worst-case spur, 60GHz operation

th: Fast-settling low-spur mmWave LO for JCAS

t: 6.7 A 10b Source-Driver IC with All-Channel Automatic Offset Calibration and Slew-Rate-Enhanced Amplifier Achieving 2273pm2/Channel and 1.9mV DVO for 6285-PPI OLED-on-Silicon Displays
pb: Microdisplays for AR/VR (4K×4K, >120Hz refresh) require compact, high-pixel-density source-driver ICs; OLED-on-Silicon (OLEDoS) integrates pixel/driving circuits on silicon but demands tight area budgets (2273pm²/ch) and low display voltage offset (DVO) for color fidelity.
me: 10-bit source-driver IC with all-channel automatic offset calibration and slew-rate-enhanced amplifier on OLEDoS backplane; achieves 2273pm²/channel area and 1.9mV DVO for 6285 PPI display through integrated low-area calibration and fast-slew output stage.
nv: First OLEDoS source driver achieving sub-pJ-energy area footprint (2273pm²/ch) with automatic per-channel calibration, enabling high-resolution (6285 PPI) AR/VR microdisplays without external trimming overhead.
th: Compact automatic-calibration source driver for ultra-high-PPI OLEDoS

t: 32.5 A 2W 53.2%-Peak-Efficiency Multi-Core Isolated DC-DC Converter with Embedded Magnetic-Core Transformer Achieving CISPR-32 Class-B EMI Compliance and <5mV Ripple
pb: Integrated isolated DC-DC converters suffer from severe conducted EMI (150kHz-30MHz) and radiated EMI (30MHz-1GHz) due to PWM control and common-mode currents across transformer parasitic capacitance, requiring bulky filters and reducing power delivery efficiency at 1W scale.
me: The converter employs a multi-core design with symmetrical inverter structure and embedded on-chip/package transformer to suppress common-mode current. It integrates PWM-controlled tens-of-MHz inverter with ~1MHz voltage regulation loop, using transformer architecture optimized for both EMI suppression and ripple reduction, achieving sub-5mV output ripple and CISPR-32 Class-B compliance.
nv: Multi-core isolated DC-DC converter design with embedded magnetic transformer achieving simultaneous EMI compliance and efficiency optimization in a monolithic integrated approach.
th: integrated EMI-compliant isolated power conversion

t: A Wireless Adiabatic Stimulator System with Current-Mode Power Reception and Stimulus Current Regulation Achieving Precise Charge Delivery and Electrode Scalability for Miniaturized Electroceuticals
pb: Miniaturized wireless neurostimulators must deliver precise charge with high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and high stimulation efficiency factor (SEF) while maintaining electrode scalability; as receiver coil shrinks, received power decreases, and electrode-tissue impedance (ETI) increases, degrading both PCE and charge delivery accuracy.
me: Current-mode power receiver with integrated stimulus current regulation achieves dual objectives: (1) direct current-mode conversion maintains high efficiency across variable ETI without requiring separate voltage regulation; (2) closed-loop stimulus current feedback provides precise charge delivery independent of electrode impedance variation. Design inherently supports electrode scalability by tolerating high ETI voltages (V_T) while maintaining constant output current regardless of load impedance.
nv: Current-mode receiver with integrated feedback-regulated stimulus delivery enabling high PCE and SEF across electrode-impedance variations without requiring impedance-adaptive design.
th: current-mode miniaturized wireless neurostimulation with ETI-scalable charge regulation

t: A 74W/48V Monolithic-GaN Integrated Adjustable Multilevel Supply Modulator for 5G Base-Station Massive-MIMO Arrays
pb: 5G and 6G base-station transmitters require efficient power management for RF power amplifiers in massive-MIMO arrays. Analog envelope tracking (AET) has limitations in bandwidth, modulation complexity, and high-voltage applications.
