Digital envelope tracking (DET) separates voltage generation (slow, efficient) and tracking (fast) stages but conventional architectures lack efficient multilevel voltage generation.
me: Monolithic GaN-based adjustable multilevel supply modulator implementing digital envelope tracking architecture. Separates voltage generation (VG) stage producing multiple voltage levels efficiently at slow rates, and tracker (TR) stage for fast voltage adjustment. Multilevel architecture reduces voltage ripple and losses vs. binary switching. 48V operation at 74W power delivery for base-station class PA supply. GaN integration achieves high efficiency and thermal performance on single die.
nv: Monolithic GaN multilevel supply modulator separating slow voltage generation and fast voltage tracking for efficient DET in base-station PAs.
th: monolithic GaN multilevel supply modulator for efficient 5G base-station DET

t: A 12A 89.3% Peak Efficiency and 26mV Undershoot 12-to-1V Two-Stage Converter with Regulated Resonant Switched-Capacitor Regulators
pb: Power converters for data centers and processors require large output current (12A) at sub-1V supply voltages, while achieving high efficiency, low undershoot, and fast transient response across wide voltage ranges (12V to 1V).
me: Two-stage regulation architecture: an intermediate bus converter (IBC) steps 12V to intermediate voltage with high efficiency, followed by a switched-capacitor point-of-load converter with regulated resonant operation achieving 89.3% peak efficiency and 26mV undershoot.
nv: Integration of regulated resonant switched-capacitor architecture in the low-voltage PoL stage to achieve both high efficiency and fast transient response simultaneously.
th: efficient multi-stage power delivery for high-current compute

t: 10.4 A 2- TRX IR-UWB Transceiver with Shared Antennas Supporting Channels 5 to 12 in Compliance with IEEE 802.15.4/4z Standards
pb: IR-UWB transceivers must support multiple channels (5-12) to reduce interference in crowded 6GHz spectrum while minimizing cost through antenna sharing, but previous integrated RF switches suffer high insertion loss degrading receiver sensitivity.
me: Fully integrated 2-TRX IR-UWB transceiver with multi-channel support (channels 5-12), using integrated CMOS RF switches optimized to reduce insertion loss while supporting shared TX/RX antenna architecture per IEEE 802.15.4/4z.
nv: Optimized integrated RF switch design reducing insertion loss and noise figure degradation compared to prior CMOS implementations, enabling multi-channel shared-antenna operation.
th: integrated multi-channel IR-UWB transceiver with shared antennas

t: 9.4 A 102ns/V 94.3%-Peak-Efficiency Symbol-Power-Tracking Supply Modulator for 5G NR Power Amplifiers
pb: 5G power amplifiers require symbol-level power tracking to match instantaneous transmit power, but achieving fast voltage transitions (102ns/V) within cyclic prefix duration (1.17µs) while maintaining efficiency remains challenging.
me: Symbol-power-tracking supply modulator using split-capacitor topology with direct switching converter and auxiliary circuits to achieve 102ns/V tracking speed and 94.3% dynamic efficiency within brief cyclic-prefix intervals.
nv: Optimized split-capacitor charging architecture with pre-charging and dynamic efficiency management to achieve sub-microsecond voltage transitions required by 5G FR1 symbol periods.
th: fast symbol-level power tracking for 5G RF amplifiers

t: 24.8 A 12GS/s 9b 16× Time-Interleaved SAR ADC in 16nm FinFET
pb: RF direct sampling and phased-array applications require high-speed ADCs (>GS/s) with both high sample rate and high SNDR (>45dB), but existing designs often require multiple supply domains or complex integration schemes.
me: 16-channel time-interleaved SAR ADC architecture operating at 12GS/s with 16nm FinFET technology, using integration-friendly single 1.8V and 0.8V supply domains optimized for area and power efficiency.
nv: System-level integration using standard process supplies instead of multiple tailored domains, simplifying larger transceiver system integration while maintaining 48.1dB SNDR.
th: integration-friendly high-speed SAR ADC for RF direct sampling

t: 19.8 A 0.65V-VDD 10.4-to-11.8GHz Fractional-N Sampling PLL Achieving 73.8fsrms Jitter, -271.5dB FoMN, and -61 dBc in-Band Fractional Spur in 40nm CMOS
pb: Sub-0.7V ultra-low-voltage PLLs must achieve sub-100fs fractional-N performance, but existing DTC and DAC approaches face voltage-headroom limitations, nonlinearity, and noise folding at low supplies.
me: LV fractional-N sampling PLL using coarse digital-to-time converter (LV-C-DTC) + fine resistor-based DAC (R-FDAC) with hybrid cascaded digital predistortion (HC-DPD) compensating nonlinearity of both DTC and sampling phase detector (SPD), plus negative-level-inverter (NL-INV) SPD reducing noise at low voltage.
nv: HC-DPD technique reducing nonlinearity compensation overhead while minimizing noise folding; NL-INV SPD enabling low-voltage operation with improved voltage headroom.
th: ultra-low-voltage fractional-N sampling PLL with smart predistortion

t: 27.5: A 4, 100µm2 Wire-Metal-Based Temperature Sensor with a Fractional-Discharge FLL and a Time-Domain Amplifier with ±0.2°C Inaccuracy (3σ) from -40 to 125°C and 45fJ·K2 Resolution FoM in 28nm CMOS
pb: Resistance-based temperature sensors must achieve compact area (<5000µm²), high accuracy (±0.2°C, 3σ), and superior resolution FoM while operating across wide temperature ranges in advanced low-VDD processes.
me: Resistor-based temperature sensor using wire-metal sensing element with fractional-discharge FLL (frequency-locked loop) and time-domain amplifier for sensitive measurement, eliminating biasing constraints of active-device sensors.
nv: Time-domain amplification and fractional-discharge FLL architecture enabling high-accuracy compact measurement without active biasing, exploiting passive resistor stability.
th: compact integrated resistive temperature sensor with time-domain amplification

t: 6.1 A 3-Stacked Hybrid-Shutter CMOS Image Sensor with Switchable 1.2µm-Pitch 50Mpixel Rolling Shutter and 2.4µm-Pitch 12.5Mpixel Global Shutter Modes for Mobile Applications
pb: Rolling-shutter CMOS image sensors achieve high pixel density but suffer flicker artifacts and motion distortion, while global-shutter sensors eliminate these issues but exhibit higher random noise due to sampling capacitor design, forcing a choice rather than flexibility.
me: 3-layer stacked CMOS image sensor combining tight 1.2µm pixel pitch rolling-shutter (50Mp) with switchable 2.4µm pixel pitch global-shutter (12.5Mp) mode using hybrid shutter architecture and advanced stacking process.
nv: Hybrid-shutter mode switching within single sensor enabling both high-resolution rolling-shutter and lower-resolution global-shutter on demand, rather than separate designs.
th: switchable hybrid-shutter image sensor for flexible mobile photography

t: An 85-to-230VAC to 3.3-to-4.6VDc 1.52W Capacitor-Drop Sigma-Floating-SC AC-DC Converter with 81.3% Peak Efficiency
pb: IoT and smart-home devices require high-efficiency, low-cost, compact non-isolated AC-DC converters for AC mains to battery-voltage output with large voltage conversion ratios (VCR). Traditional inductive switching converters are bulky; linear regulators are inefficient. Switched-capacitor approaches have poor output power scaling and lack voltage regulation.
me: A sigma-floating switched-capacitor (SC) architecture with capacitor-drop AC-DC topology and three-mode active rectifier regulation. Capacitive division blocks high AC voltage using series capacitors, reducing stress on integrated converter stages. A semi-active or three-mode active rectifier adjusts current to maintain regulated DC output while minimizing idle-phase losses compared to prior two-phase designs.
nv: Sigma-floating switched-capacitor architecture enabling regulated output power at >1W from AC mains with 81.3% efficiency, surpassing prior passive capacitive and SC-LDO hybrid approaches.
th: Sigma-floating switched-capacitor AC-DC converter for integrated IoT power delivery

t: 7.10 An 8-to-28GHz 8-Phase Clock Generator Using Dual-Feedback Ring Oscillator in 28nm CMOS
pb: Multi-phase clock generation for high-speed wireline transceivers (>224Gb/s PAM-4) requires low jitter and phase error across wide frequency range (8–28GHz); PLL-based approaches become costly at fT limits of 200–300GHz CMOS processes.
me: Dual-feedback ring oscillator: cascades DLL (delay-locked loop) with ring oscillator (RO) injection-locked by the DLL. DLL expands input clock to multiple phases; RO's autonomous feedback suppresses phase error and reduces jitter compared to standalone DLL while maintaining wide frequency tuning.
nv: Dual-feedback architecture combining DLL phase expansion with RO injection-locking to achieve both low phase error and low jitter across 8–28GHz range without PLL-divider overhead.

mx.jitter: low (exact values not provided in abstract)

th: Dual-feedback clock generation for multi-phase wideband synthesis

t: HOOP: A Scalable Hybrid DC-DC Converter Ring for High-Performance Computing
pb: Multi-phase DC-DC converters for AI-era HPC require automatic current balancing across tens or hundreds of phases without complex digital control; hybrid topologies in parallel remain difficult to balance between converters.
me: HOOP: Hybrid converter with power ring (Φ0) for auto current balance and back ring (Φ0) for phase shedding. Leverages charge-balance properties of capacitors (similar to prior buck/three-level approaches) but extends to parallel hybrid converters via ring topology for inter-converter balancing.
nv: Ring topology enabling inherent auto-current-balancing across multiple hybrid DC-DC converters without dedicated digital controller.
th: Scalable auto-balancing power delivery via converter rings

t: 33.2 A 216-to-226GHz Watt-Level GaN Solid-State Power Amplifier with Multiband Large-Signal Impedance Correction and Circuit-Package Co-Design Technique
pb: 220GHz solid-state power amplifiers (SSPAs) are critical for future high-data-rate wireless, imaging, and radar; Si (CMOS/SiGe) and III-V (GaAs/InP) PAs suffer from low operating voltage (<2V single device), requiring low impedance at output (high current), limiting bandwidth and power density. GaN HEMTs offer higher voltage/current ratings but design is challenging at G-band.
me: GaN HEMT-based 216–226GHz SSPA using: (1) multiband large-signal impedance correction to optimize output impedance across the G-band range despite device parasitics, (2) circuit-package co-design enabling efficient coupling from PA to antenna/load while managing thermal and parasitic effects.
nv: GaN SSPA with multiband impedance correction and circuit-package co-design achieving watt-level output power at 220GHz.
th: GaN-HEMT watt-level PA for 220GHz wireless/imaging

t: A 232-to-260GHz CMOS Amplifier-Multiplier Chain With a Low-Cost, Matching-Sheet-Assisted Radiation Package and 11.1dBm Total Radiated Power
pb: Compact CMOS terahertz (THz) sources are limited by low radiated power (several mW); on-chip radiation via front-side patch antennas suffers low efficiency (~25%) and narrow bandwidth (~5%); back-side radiation improves efficiency but requires expensive silicon lenses (cm-sized, high-cost assembly) to overcome total internal reflection at Si-air interface.
me: 232–260GHz CMOS amplifier-multiplier chain with back-side radiation via low-cost patterned dielectric matching sheet (instead of silicon lens). Matching sheet enhances wave coupling from silicon (εr=11.9) to air (εr=1), improving radiation efficiency and bandwidth. Circuit uses high-power FinFET (HyPowerFF) technology and broadband gain-peaking power amplifiers.
nv: Patterned dielectric matching sheet replacing expensive silicon lenses for efficient back-side THz radiation, enabling low-cost CMOS THz source packaging.
th: Low-cost CMOS terahertz source via matching-sheet radiation

t: 4.3 A 0.36nW, 820µm², 32kHz Conduction-Angle-Adaptive Crystal Oscillator in 28nm CMOS for Real-Time Clock Applications
pb: 32.768kHz crystal oscillators (XOs) for real-time clocks consume 10-100nW, and pulse-injection XOs (PIXOs) achieving sub-nW power still require separate start-up circuits and face robustness challenges under interference.
me: Conduction-angle-adaptive crystal oscillator in 28nm CMOS with tiny conduction-angle pulse injection (Class-C-like operation) that eliminates the need for separate start-up circuits and provides robust oscillation initiation without additional control logic.
nv: Conduction-angle-adaptive mechanism that enables self-starting oscillation without separate start-up circuitry.
th: Self-starting ultra-low-power crystal oscillator

t: 27.3 A Sub-1V 14b 5.8nW/Hz BW/Power-Scalable CT Sensor Interface with a Frequency-Controlled Current Source Achieving a 225× Scalable Range
pb: Sensor interfaces for weak signals (tens of mV: shunt current sensors, biomedical) require low noise and scalable bandwidth/power for different IoT applications; discrete-time ADCs suffer from kT/C noise, while continuous-time front-ends consume fixed power.
me: Continuous-time (CT) sensor interface using frequency-controlled current source that enables scalable bandwidth and power dissipation across a 225× range. CT front-stage suppresses kT/C sampling noise while frequency tuning allows bandwidth-power trade-offs.
nv: Frequency-controlled current source enabling wide power-bandwidth scalability (225×) in continuous-time sensor interface.
th: Scalable continuous-time sensor interface for IoT

t: 32.1 A 180MHz 45.3%-Peak-Efficiency Isolated Converter Using Q-Downsize Class-D Power Amplifier with Inherent Shoot-Through Current Blocking and High Tolerance for Efficiency Despite Frequency Misalignments
pb: Isolated DC-DC converters suffer from high electromagnetic interference (EMI) due to common-mode (CM) current across the isolation barrier; suppressing CM voltage variation requires fully symmetrical transmitter (TX) topologies but introduces complexity.
me: Class-D power amplifier with Q-downsize technique that inherently blocks shoot-through current, combined with fully symmetrical TX topology and coil routing in opposite directions to cancel magnetic field, achieving 45.3% peak efficiency at 180MHz with high tolerance to frequency variations.
nv: Q-downsize Class-D topology with inherent shoot-through blocking, eliminating dead-time complexity while maintaining efficiency across frequency misalignments.
th: High-efficiency isolated converter with robustness to misalignment

t: A 6.78MHz 94.2% Peak Efficiency Class-E Transmitter with Adaptive Real-Part Impedance Matching and Imaginary-Part Phase Compensation Achieving a 33W Wireless-Power-Transfer System
pb: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems achieve high efficiency only at specific load points; load impedance varies significantly as charging state changes, causing both real and imaginary parts to shift beyond the circuit's operating range.
me: Class-E power amplifier at 6.78MHz with dual adaptive impedance matching: real-part adaptation via dynamic impedance matching network, and imaginary-part phase compensation via adaptive capacitance (avoiding nonlinear MOS capacitors), achieving 94.2% peak efficiency across wide load range.
nv: Separate adaptive control of real and imaginary parts of load impedance, with integrated tunable elements avoiding nonlinear MOS capacitors.
th: Adaptive dual-impedance Class-E WPT transmitter

t: Reversing Scattering to Perform Deep-Tissue Optical Imaging and the Current Need for a Suitable Optoelectronic Solution
pb: Biological tissues are highly turbid (mean optical scattering length ~100 microns), preventing high-resolution optical imaging and excitation beyond ~1mm depth; traditional deep-penetrating modalities (X-ray, MRI, ultrasound) lack biochemical sensitivity.
me: Optical scattering-reversal approach that compensates for tissue turbidity by reversing the scattering process, enabling focused light delivery and collection through deep tissue, requiring novel optoelectronic integrated circuits for signal modulation and detection.
nv: Scattering-reversal optical technique to overcome tissue turbidity, enabling deep-tissue high-resolution biochemical imaging.
th: Scattering-reversed deep-tissue optical imaging

t: A 17.7-to-29.5GHz Transceiver Front-End with 3.3dB NF and 20.2dBm OP1dB in 65nm CMOS
pb: Wideband mm-wave transceivers must simultaneously achieve low-noise wideband RX, high-efficiency wideband TX, and excellent TX/RX isolation for 5G, LEO SATCOM, and JSAC applications. These three requirements interact and conflict with conventional designs.
me: The design integrates a wideband RX front-end (3.3dB NF), wideband TX path (20.2dBm OP1dB), and TX/RX isolation circuitry in a single 65nm CMOS process, operating across the 17.7-29.5GHz band via frequency tuning.
nv: Simultaneous integration of low-noise RX, high-efficiency TX, and isolation in a single wideband mm-wave transceiver without requiring separate narrowband designs.
th: wideband mm-wave transceiver integration

t: 21.3 A Segmented-Interlacing Multi-Phase Hybrid Converter with Inherently Auto-Balanced ILs and Boosted IL Slew Rate During Load Transients
pb: Multi-phase buck/hybrid converters suffer from inductor current imbalance due to duty-cycle mismatches, requiring per-phase current sensing and closed-loop adjustment. Low inductor slew rate creates large output voltage undershoot during load transients.
me: Segmented-interlacing multi-phase hybrid converter with inherent auto-balancing via duty-cycle compensation and simultaneous energization of all inductors during load transients to boost slew rate, eliminating per-phase current sensing.
nv: Inherent inductor current auto-balancing without per-phase sensing, achieved through segmented architecture and dual-mode control.
th: auto-balanced multi-phase power converter

t: 11.2 A Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with VCO-Based Non-Uniform Multi-Level Time-Approximation Filter with -36dB EVM in 28nm CMOS
pb: Crowded spectrum creates out-of-band (OOB) and alias-band blockers that degrade in-band EVM after sampling. Prior time-approximation-filtering (TAF) and N-path filter designs have limited blocker rejection and reconfigurability.
me: Mixer-first receiver combining multilevel time-approximation filtering (mTAF), VCO-based integrator with embedded digitalization, and non-uniform sampling with N-path filtering. Time-gated integration patterns suppress multiple blocker types simultaneously.
nv: Multilevel TAF with VCO-based integrator providing 65dB blocker rejection while maintaining high reconfigurability and low implementation cost.
th: blocker-tolerant receiver with multi-level time-approximation filtering

t: 18.5 A Rail-to-Rail 3rd-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC Achieving 105.4dB SFDR with Integrated Input Buffer Using Continuous-Time Correlated Level Shifting
pb: High-resolution SAR ADCs (>13b) require large capacitive DACs to meet kT/C noise specs, heavily loading the input buffer. Buffer driving large CDAC while achieving rail-to-rail swing and linearity dominates power consumption, becoming the efficiency bottleneck.
me: Rail-to-rail SAR ADC with continuous-time correlated level shifting in the input buffer, integrating the buffer into the noise-shaping loop. Level shifting bias compensates for signal swing while maintaining linearity, avoiding need for higher supply voltage.
nv: Continuous-time correlated level shifting seamlessly integrating rail-to-rail input buffer into SAR noise-shaping loop without requiring separate higher supply voltage.
th: integrated input buffer SAR ADC with noise-shaping

t: 3.2 A 36V Current-Balancing Instrumentation Amplifier with ±24V Input Range, 5.6MHz BW, and 140dB CMRR at All Gain Settings
pb: Industrial instrumentation amplifiers must handle large differential input ranges (>20V) with large common-mode input offsets (±10V), require high CMRR (>120dB), high input impedance (>10MΩ), and wide bandwidth while processing millivolt-level signals from sensors.
me: 36V high-voltage instrumentation amplifier with current-balancing architecture enabling ±24V differential input range and ±10V CM input handling. Direct coupling with carefully designed gain stages maintains 140dB CMRR across all gain settings.
nv: Current-balancing topology achieving 140dB CMRR at all gain settings without requiring separate higher supply voltage for CM rejection.
th: high-voltage instrumentation amplifier with superior CMRR

t: An 18.5nF-Input-Range PM-SAR-Hybrid Capacitance-to-Digital Converter Achieving 6.1µs Conversion Time at 18.1pF Input Capacitance
pb: Capacitive sensors require wide-input-range (>10nF), fast-conversion (<10µs), high-resolution CDCs. SAR and ΔΣM CDCs offer energy efficiency but suffer from limited input range due to analog saturation. Period-modulation (PM) CDCs achieve wide range but incur long conversion times counting oscillation periods.
me: PM-SAR-Hybrid CDC combining period modulation (for wide range via time-domain operation) with SAR conversion (for fast resolution), eliminating saturation limits while achieving sub-10µs conversion. SAR post-processing counts/resolves PM oscillation cycles efficiently.
nv: Hybrid PM-SAR topology combining wide-range period-modulation with fast-conversion SAR, overcoming traditional range-vs-speed trade-off.
th: hybrid PM-SAR capacitance-to-digital converter with wide range

t: A 0.024mm2 All-Digital Fractional Output Divider with 257fs Worst-Case Jitter Using Split-DTC-Based Background Calibration
pb: Fractional output dividers (FODs) using digital-to-time converters (DTCs) suffer from PVT variations, gain errors, and integral nonlinearity (INL), degrading jitter performance significantly. Prior calibration methods require additional reference clocks or auxiliary PLLs, increasing area and complexity.
me: All-digital FOD using split-DTC-based background calibration measuring and correcting both DTC gain and INL errors without requiring reference clock or auxiliary PLL. Split DTCs enable self-referential gain and INL calibration.
nv: Split-DTC-based background calibration enabling simultaneous gain and INL compensation without external reference or auxiliary PLL.
th: compact all-digital fractional divider with split-DTC calibration

t: A Blocker-Tolerant mm-Wave Low-Noise Amplifier Utilizing Doherty Active Load Modulation for Linearity Enhancement
pb: Emerging mm-wave applications (massive MIMO, automotive radar, SATCOM-on-the-Move, AR/VR) require high-linearity receivers/LNAs to handle multiple concurrent signals or weak signals amid strong interferers. Conventional LNA designs optimize for noise at weak signals but cannot maintain linearity with strong blockers.
me: Blocker-tolerant mm-wave LNA leveraging Doherty active load modulation to enhance linearity across wide input power range. Doherty architecture dynamically adjusts gain vs. linearity trade-off, maintaining output power efficiency under strong blockers.
nv: Doherty active load modulation applied to mm-wave LNA design enabling simultaneous high linearity and low noise in presence of strong interferers.
th: Doherty-modulated mm-wave LNA for blocker tolerance

t: 28.2 A 189.3dB-FoMs 14.5fJ/Conversion-Step Continuous-Time Noise-Shaping SAR Capacitance-to-Digital Converter
pb: High-resolution capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) for IoT environmental monitoring (humidity, pressure) face kT/C and flicker noise limits. ΔΣM-based CDCs offer high resolution via oversampling/noise-shaping but power consumption remains limited by noise floor.
me: Continuous-time ΔΣM-based CDC using noise-shaping to achieve high resolution while oversampling, directly working in capacitance domain. CT architecture avoids sampling-clock jitter and enables continuous signal processing.
nv: Continuous-time noise-shaping SAR CDC architecture achieving high resolution with superior figure-of-merit (FoM) via CT integration.
th: continuous-time noise-shaping CDC for IoT sensing

t: 5.6 A Power-Efficient CORDIC-Less Digital Polar Transmitter Using 1b DSM-Based PA Supporting 256-QAM
pb: Digital polar transmitters require CORDIC for I/Q-to-polar conversion but CORDIC's nonlinearity causes bandwidth expansion of AM/PM outputs, challenging wideband implementations. Switched-capacitor PAs suffer low efficiency at power backoff; existing AM/PM modulation methods (PI, DTC, VMD SCPA) introduce further nonlinearity requiring complex DPD.
me: CORDIC-less digital polar transmitter using intrinsically linear 1-bit PA directly supporting polar AM/PM. Edge-selection-based phase modulation replaces CORDIC. 1-bit DSM-based PA inherently avoids switch-capacitor losses and maintains linearity without digital pre-distortion.
nv: CORDIC-less architecture using 1-bit DSM PA with edge-selection phase modulation, eliminating CORDIC nonlinearity and achieving linearity without DPD.
th: CORDIC-less polar transmitter with 1-bit DSM PA

t: 10.1 A 77GHz Hybrid TDMA-MIMO Phased-Array Radar with 186m Detection Range and 3cm Range Resolution
pb: Current MIMO and phased-array radar architectures cannot simultaneously achieve long-range detection (LRR >250m), medium-range (MRR, 3-30m), and short-range (SRR, <10m) with optimal resolution for all three modes. Existing designs trade off maximum range vs. range/angular resolution across driving modes.
me: A fully integrated 77GHz hybrid TDMA-MIMO phased-array FMCW radar with 8 transmitters and 8 receivers (2x4 array) employs different chirp profiles to dynamically support LRR, MRR, and SRR detection modes. TDMA (time-division) interleaves with MIMO beamforming to achieve both long-range and fine angular resolution.
nv: Hybrid TDMA-MIMO architecture enabling all three radar detection modes (LRR/MRR/SRR) from a single integrated design using adaptive chirp profiling.
th: Unified multi-mode FMCW radar via hybrid TDMA-MIMO

t: 26.4 A 24-to-29GHz Compact Transmit/Receive Front-End Module Featuring an Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier and 0.22mm2 Area
pb: Mm-wave FEMs must simultaneously achieve high TX linearity/efficiency and low RX noise figure while remaining compact. Conventional Class-AB PAs provide <10% TX PAE under OFDM signals with 10dB PAPR, limiting overall system efficiency.
me: An asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (DPA) design provides high efficiency under modulated signals through dynamic bias adjustment and impedance modulation. The FEM integrates PA, LNA, and T/R switch in a 0.22mm² footprint for 24-29GHz operation.
nv: Asymmetric Doherty PA architecture achieving high PAE under OFDM waveforms while maintaining compact integration in a small FEM form factor.
th: Asymmetric Doherty PA for compact mm-wave FEMs

t: 24.5 A 72GS/s 9b Time-Interleaved Pipeline-SAR ADC Achieving 55.3/49.3dB SFDR at 20GHz/Nyquist Inputs in 16nm FinFET
pb: Time-interleaved (TI) ADCs for optical receivers (>100Gb/s) require near-100GS/s sampling with high SFDR (>55dB) at wideband (>20GHz) inputs. Massive TI factors degrade SFDR due to bandwidth mismatch and implicit distortion in the interleaver; sampling-capacitor tuning addresses only first-order correction; high-frequency input buffers introduce distortion and gain attenuation.
me: A 72GS/s 9b time-interleaved pipeline-SAR ADC employs linearized wideband input buffers, dual-path bootstrapped switches (BS), and R/R-based open-loop amplifier to minimize inter-stage gain (ISG) calibration complexity. The pipeline-SAR architecture combines pipeline linearity with SAR efficiency at 1.125GS/s per unit, scaled to 72GS/s via 64-fold time interleaving.
nv: Pipeline-SAR TI architecture with linearized input buffers and bootstrapped switching achieving >55dB SFDR at 20GHz inputs without ISG calibration.
th: TI pipeline-SAR ADC for high-SFDR optical receivers

t: Spatial-Temporal Direct-Digital Beamforming Power Amplifier with Enhanced Back-Off Efficiency in a 24GHz Phased Array
pb: mm-Wave transmitters face degraded back-off efficiency when transmitting high-order constellations (PAPR 7-9.5dB for 5G+) while requiring efficient beamforming. Traditional architectures address beamforming and power back-off (PBO) separately—baseband beamforming increases complexity; RF beamforming suffers mismatch and insertion loss.
me: The Spatial-Temporal Beamforming Power Amplifier (ST-BPA) integrates direct-digital amplitude-and-phase beamforming with power back-off operation in a unified mm-wave PA architecture. This combined approach can be augmented with efficiency-enhancement techniques (Doherty, envelope tracking, or outphasing) to further improve back-off performance across the phased array.
nv: Direct-digital spatial-temporal beamforming PA unifying amplitude/phase control and power back-off without separate baseband or RF stages.
th: Integrated spatial-temporal PA beamforming for efficiency

t: A Reference-Less CDR Using SAR-Based Frequency-Acquisition Technique Achieving 55ns Constant Band-Searching Time and up to 63.64Gb/s/µs Acquisition Speed
pb: Reference-less CDR circuits used in burst-traffic systems suffer slow frequency acquisition (FA), which is the primary bottleneck for link wake-up latency. Dynamic data-center traffic requires frequent sleep-to-wake transitions; existing CDRs have multi-microsecond FA times that dominate link setup delay.
me: A reference-less CDR employs successive-approximation-register (SAR) based frequency band-switching to achieve constant 55ns band-search time. A novel charge pump (CP) with positive net current enables rapid frequency convergence. Total FA time <150ns is achieved through combined SAR band-switching and refined frequency tuning.
nv: SAR-based frequency-band switching for reference-less CDR achieving constant-time fast FA without external frequency reference.

mx.other: 55ns band-search time, <150ns total FA time, 63.64Gb/s/µs acquisition speed

th: Fast SAR-based reference-less CDR for burst traffic

t: A 6.78MHz Single-Stage Regulating Rectifier with Dual Outputs Simultaneously Charged in a Half Cycle Achieving 92.2% Efficiency and 131mW Output Power
pb: Wireless power transfer (WPT) to implanted biomedical devices requires efficient power conditioning, and implants often need multiple output voltages (e.g., low voltage for biopotential recording, high voltage for neurostimulation) with different performance requirements (stability vs. bandwidth). Single-output rectifiers cannot simultaneously meet these conflicting demands.
me: Single-stage regulating rectifier with dual simultaneous outputs per half-cycle at 6.78MHz switching frequency. The architecture achieves independent regulation of two output voltages: low stable voltage (V_OUT2) for recording front-end and high-bandwidth voltage (V_OUT1) for stimulation back-end, within a single rectifier stage rather than cascading multiple stages.
nv: Single-stage rectifier topology enabling simultaneous dual-output charging and independent regulation in a half-cycle to meet conflicting voltage/bandwidth requirements of implant power delivery.
th: Efficient single-stage dual-output rectifier for implanted biomedical devices

t: Interleaved Bitstream Execution for Multi-Pattern Regex Matching on GPUs
pb: Bitparallel regex engines compile regular expressions into bitstream programs that expose fine-grained instruction-level parallelism well-suited for GPU execution, but the naive sequential (per-instruction loop-over-data) execution model suffers from poor data reuse — each data block is loaded multiple times across instructions — and high memory consumption from intermediate bitstream state, limiting GPU throughput.
me: The paper introduces an interleaved bitstream execution model in which all bitstream instructions for all patterns are fused into a single loop body executed block-wise, so each data block is loaded once and processed by all instructions before moving to the next. Three key techniques make this practical on GPUs: (1) Dependency-Aware Thread-Data Mapping that resolves cross-block data dependencies — introduced because instructions in later iterations depend on state from prior blocks — via selective recomputation of dependency chains rather than communication; (2) Shift Rebalancing that restructures dependency chains to reduce the depth of synchronization barriers needed between warp threads; and (3) Zero Block Skipping that exploits bitstream sparsity (many blocks evaluate to all-zero intermediate state) to skip computation on zero blocks, reducing total work.
nv: An interleaved execution model that fuses all bitstream regex instructions into a single data-block-wise loop, improving data reuse and eliminating intermediate memory traffic, with dependency resolution via selective recomputation instead of inter-thread communication.

mx.speedup: 19.5x geometric mean speedup over state-of-the-art GPU regex engine

th: Interleaved bitstream execution for GPU regex pattern matching

t: Photon: Federated LLM Pre-Training
pb: LLM pre-training is constrained to high-bandwidth data centers because standard distributed training (3D parallelism) requires AllReduce at every step, making cross-region or internet-scale collaboration impractical due to low inter-datacenter bandwidth.
me: Photon is a federated LLM pre-training system using cross-silo FL with LocalSGD. Each client performs many local gradient steps before synchronizing. The system exploits federated averaging's robustness to enable small local batch sizes with high learning rates—a combination that improves generalization via noise injection. Architecture includes an Aggregator (central server), LLM Clients (local training nodes), and Data Sources. Communication uses parameter server, AllReduce, or Ring-AllReduce depending on network topology. Adaptive local parallelism selects DDP/FSDP vs sub-federation based on client connectivity.
nv: First complete system for federated LLM pre-training at billion-parameter scale that trains models matching or exceeding centralized training quality, exploiting federated averaging's robustness to combine small batch sizes with high learning rates for 2x faster convergence than DiLoCo.

mx.speedup: 35% wall-time reduction vs centralized for 7B model (95.6h vs 147.9h at 10Gbps with Ring-AllReduce)
mx.other: Communication reduced 500x for 7B model; 64-512x less overall

th: Distributed LLM training

t: Scaling Deep Learning Training with MPMD Pipeline Parallelism
pb: GSPMD/SPMD-based pipeline parallelism in JAX can only encode GPipe-style schedules; it cannot express MPMD schedules like 1F1B or Interleaved 1F1B that improve memory efficiency and throughput, and it forces homogeneous stages with poor scalability over low-bandwidth (DCN) inter-node links.
me: JaxPP extends JAX with a MPMD pipeline parallelism runtime. Users annotate model code with pipeline_yield calls that mark stage boundaries; JaxPP infers stages from data dependencies. An accumulate_grads API implements the gradient accumulation loop with user-specified schedules (1F1B, Interleaved 1F1B). A single-controller driver process traces the JAX computation to a task graph, assigns tasks to SPMD actors (each actor manages one or more devices with a local SPMD mesh), and infers send/receive pairs using topological ordering to avoid deadlocks. Buffer deletion is handled by a liveness pass. All task dispatches are fused into a single RPC per actor. A loop commuting pass handles weight sharing (tied embeddings) efficiently.
nv: First JAX-native MPMD pipeline parallelism system that supports arbitrary user-defined pipeline schedules (including 1F1B and Interleaved 1F1B) via lightweight pipeline_yield annotations, without requiring model rewrites, while remaining fully model-agnostic through XLA compilation.
hw: NVIDIA H100 GPUs (DGX H100 nodes), InfiniBand NDR400 interconnect; multi-node clusters
th: Distributed Training & Parallelism

t: The Hidden Bloat in Machine Learning Systems
pb: ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, MXNet) ship highly bloated shared libraries with large amounts of unused GPU and CPU code, wasting memory, increasing load times, and degrading performance.
me: Negativa-ML hooks the CUDA cuModuleGetFunction API to detect which GPU kernel functions are actually called at runtime per workload. GPU code is localized at the cubin (binary) and element (function) granularity. CPU code analysis uses existing call-graph techniques. Unused GPU cubins and functions are removed from the shared libraries. Evaluated across 4 ML frameworks, 10 workloads, and 300+ shared libraries.
nv: First tool to identify and remove GPU code bloat from ML shared libraries using cuModuleGetFunction hook for runtime kernel detection, revealing that GPU code is the primary source of bloat and hardware-architecture mismatch is its root cause.
th: ML System Optimization / Software Debloating

t: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
pb: AdamW optimizer for LLM training maintains first and second moments, tripling memory requirements over model weights alone (28 GB optimizer states for LLaMA-7B). This forces smaller batch sizes, more GPUs, or lower-end models.
me: APOLLO identifies that AdamW's element-wise learning rate adaptation can be coarsened to channel-wise or tensor-wise scaling without performance loss. It approximates channel-wise gradient scaling factors using an auxiliary low-rank optimizer state in a random-projected space (not SVD). Algorithm: (1) project full gradient to low-rank space via random Gaussian matrix; (2) apply AdamW on the low-rank gradient to get low-rank moments; (3) extract channel-wise scaling factors from low-rank moments; (4) apply scaling to full gradient for weight update. APOLLO-Mini uses tensor-wise (rank-1) scaling for SGD-level memory. The random projection matrix is resampled every T=200 steps. A Norm-growth Limiter stabilizes training.
nv: Theoretical proof (via Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma) that random projection preserves gradient scaling factors up to a bounded ratio, enabling SVD-free low-rank approximation that is rank-insensitive and achieves SGD-level memory at AdamW performance.
wl: LLaMA pre-training (60M to 7B) on C4 dataset
Fine-tuning on commonsense reasoning (LLaMA-3.2-1B, LLaMA-3-8B, Gemma-7B, Mistral-7B)

mx.perplexity_vs_adamw_llama1b: APOLLO-Mini achieves lower perplexity than AdamW at 2.60G vs 7.80G optimizer memory
mx.throughput_improvement: ~3x on LLaMA-7B (8xA100) via 4x larger batch sizes
mx.perplexity_improvement_vs_galore: Up to 3.62 points better at same memory budget

th: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimizer / Training Efficiency
